title.en: Volume 245 Biographies 133: Zhou Qiyuan, Miao Changqi, Zhou Shunchang, Zhou Zongjian, Huang Zunsu, Li Yingsheng, Wan Jing
title.raw: 卷二百四十五 列傳第一百三十三 周起元 繆昌期 周順昌 周宗建 黃尊素 李應昇 萬燝 Volume 245 Biographies 133: Zhou Qiyuan, Miao Changqi, Zhou Shunchang, Zhou Zongjian, Huang Zunsu, Li Yingsheng, Wan Jing

sentences.zh: 周起元繆昌期周順昌

translations.literal: Zhou Qiyuan, Miao Changqi, Zhou Shunchang
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiyuan, Miao Changqi, Zhou Shunchang

translations.literal: (Sub-biographies: Zi Maolan, Zhu Zuweng, Yan Peiwei, and others)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Sub-biographies: Zi Maolan, Zhu Zuweng, Yan Peiwei, and others)〉

sentences.zh: 周宗建

translations.literal: Zhou Zongjian
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zongjian

sentences.zh: （蔣英）〉

translations.literal: (Jiang Ying)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Jiang Ying)〉

sentences.zh: 黃尊素李應升萬燝

translations.literal: Huang Zunsu, Li Yingsheng, Wan Jing
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zunsu, Li Yingsheng, Wan Jing

sentences.zh: （丁乾學等）〉

translations.literal: (Ding Qianxue and others)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ding Qianxue and others)〉

sentences.zh: 周起元，字仲先，海澄人。

translations.literal: Zhou Qiyuan, styled Zhongxian, was a native of Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiyuan, styled Zhongxian, was a native of Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十八年鄉試第一，明年成進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Wanli he ranked first in the provincial examination; the next year he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of the Wanli reign he topped the provincial examinations, and the following year he passed the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 歷知浮梁、南昌，以廉惠稱。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Fuliang and Nanchang, and was known for integrity and benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Fuliang and Nanchang, where he won renown for integrity and humane governance.

sentences.zh: 行取入都，註湖廣道御史。

translations.literal: Selected for appointment in the capital, he was registered as an investigating censor for the Huguang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen for promotion to the capital, he was slated for appointment as investigating censor of the Huguang circuit.

sentences.zh: 方候命，值京察。

translations.literal: While awaiting his commission, the capital evaluation of officials took place.
translations.idiomatic: While he was still awaiting his commission, the capital evaluation of officials was held.

sentences.zh: 御史劉國縉疑鄭繼芳假書出起元及李邦華、李炳恭、徐縉芳、徐良彥手，遂目為「五鬼」，繼芳且入之疏中。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Guojin suspected that Zheng Jifang's memorial had been forged by Qiyuan together with Li Banghua, Li Binggong, Xu Jinfang, and Xu Liangyan, and so labeled them the "Five Demons"; Zheng Jifang even put this into his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Guojin suspected that a memorial in Zheng Jifang's name had actually been drafted by Qiyuan together with Li Banghua, Li Binggong, Xu Jinfang, and Xu Liangyan, and dubbed them the "Five Demons"; Zheng Jifang even inserted the label into his own memorial.

sentences.zh: 起元憤，上章自明。

translations.literal: Qiyuan was indignant and submitted a memorial to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan was outraged and submitted a memorial to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 居二年，御史命始下。

translations.literal: After two years, his appointment as censor was finally issued.
translations.idiomatic: Only after two years was his commission as censor finally issued.

sentences.zh: 會太仆少卿徐兆魁以攻東林為御史錢春所劾，起元亦疏劾之。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Xu Zhaokui, for attacking the Donglin faction, was impeached by Censor Qian Chun; Qiyuan also memorialized in impeachment of him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Zhaokui, vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was impeached by Censor Qian Chun for attacking the Donglin faction, and Qiyuan likewise submitted a memorial impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 奸人劉世學者，誠意伯劉藎臣從祖也，疏詆顧憲成，起元憤，力斥其謬。

translations.literal: A villain named Liu Shixue, a collateral ancestor of the Marquis of Sincerity Liu Jinchen, submitted a memorial slandering Gu Xiancheng; Qiyuan was angered and forcefully refuted his absurdities.
translations.idiomatic: A scoundrel named Liu Shixue, a collateral kinsman of the Marquis of Sincerity Liu Jinchen, submitted a memorial defaming Gu Xiancheng; Qiyuan was incensed and forcefully exposed the absurdity of his charges.

sentences.zh: 藎臣遂訐起元，益詆憲成。

translations.literal: Jinchen then impeached Qiyuan and further slandered Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchen then impeached Qiyuan in turn and heaped further slander on Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 起元再疏極論，其同官翟鳳翀、余懋衡、徐良彥、魏雲中、李邦華、王時熙、潘之祥亦交章論列。

translations.literal: Qiyuan submitted a second memorial arguing to the utmost; his colleagues Zhai Fengchong, Yu Maoheng, Xu Liangyan, Wei Yunzhong, Li Banghua, Wang Shixi, and Pan Zhixiang also submitted memorials in succession discussing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan submitted a second memorial arguing the case at length, and his colleagues Zhai Fengchong, Yu Maoheng, Xu Liangyan, Wei Yunzhong, Li Banghua, Wang Shixi, and Pan Zhixiang likewise weighed in with a stream of memorials.

sentences.zh: 且下令捕世學，世學遂遁去。

translations.literal: Moreover an order was issued to arrest Shixue, and Shixue then fled.
translations.idiomatic: An order was also issued to arrest Shixue, who promptly fled.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎方從哲由中旨起官，起元力言不可，並刺給事中亓詩教、周永春，吏部侍郎李養正、郭士望等。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Fang Congzhe was restored to office by an edict from within the palace; Qiyuan forcefully argued that this should not be done, and also attacked Supervising Secretaries Qi Shijiao and Zhou Yongchun, and Vice Ministers of Personnel Li Yangzheng and Guo Shiwan, among others.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister of Personnel Fang Congzhe was reappointed by a palace edict bypassing regular channels, Qiyuan argued strenuously that this must not stand, and also took aim at supervising secretaries Qi Shijiao and Zhou Yongchun and vice ministers of personnel Li Yangzheng and Guo Shiwan, among others.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書趙煥出雲中、時熙於外，起元劾其背旨擅權，坐停俸。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan sent Yunzhong and Shixi out of the capital; Qiyuan impeached him for defying the imperial will and arrogating power, and was punished by suspension of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan posted Yunzhong and Shixi to posts outside the capital; Qiyuan impeached him for defying the throne's intent and usurping authority, and was himself penalized with suspension of salary.

sentences.zh: 煥去，鄭繼之代，又出之祥及張鍵。

translations.literal: When Huan left office, Zheng Jizhi replaced him and again sent out Zhixiang and Zhang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan left office, Zheng Jizhi took his place and again posted Zhixiang and Zhang Jian outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 起元亦抗疏糾駁，因言張光房等五人不當擯之部曹。

translations.literal: Qiyuan also submitted a defiant memorial of rebuttal, stating that Zhang Guangfang and four others should not be relegated to minor posts in the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan also submitted a defiant memorial of rebuttal, arguing that Zhang Guangfang and four others ought not to be banished to lowly posts in the ministries.

sentences.zh: 與黨人牴牾，忌者益眾。

translations.literal: He clashed with factional opponents, and those who resented him grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed repeatedly with his factional enemies, and those who bore him ill will grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 尋巡按陜西，風采甚著。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he toured and inspected Shaanxi as investigating censor, with very distinguished bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent to tour and inspect Shaanxi as investigating censor, where his authority and bearing were widely noted.

sentences.zh: 卒以東林故，出為廣西參議，分守右江道。

translations.literal: In the end, because of his Donglin affiliation, he was sent out as administration vice commissioner of Guangxi, with responsibility for guarding the Right River circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, on account of his Donglin ties, he was posted out as administration vice commissioner of Guangxi, charged with guarding the Right River circuit.

sentences.zh: 柳州大饑，群盜蜂起，起元單騎招劇賊，而振恤饑民甚至。

translations.literal: When Liuzhou suffered a great famine, bandits rose everywhere in swarms; Qiyuan went alone on horseback to win over fierce bandits, while he relieved and comforted the starving people to an extraordinary degree.
translations.idiomatic: When Liuzhou was stricken by severe famine and bandits swarmed everywhere, Qiyuan rode out alone to win over the most violent gangs, while extending relief to the starving with extraordinary thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 移四川副使，未上。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be vice commissioner of Sichuan but had not yet taken up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as vice commissioner of Sichuan but had not yet reported to his new post.

sentences.zh: 會遼陽破，廷議通州重地，宜設監司，乃命起元以參政蒞之。

translations.literal: It happened that Liaoyang fell; the court debated that Tongzhou was a vital place and ought to have a supervising official, and so ordered Qiyuan to go there as administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaoyang fell, the court debated whether Tongzhou, a place of critical importance, should have a supervising commissioner, and Qiyuan was ordered to take up the post as administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年入為太仆少卿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi he entered the capital as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Tianqi reign he was recalled to the capital as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 旋擢右僉都御史，巡撫蘇、松十府。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of the ten prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of the ten prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 公廉愛民，絲粟無所取。

translations.literal: He was upright, incorruptible, and loved the people, taking not even a thread or a grain for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, incorruptible, and devoted to the people, he would not take so much as a thread or a grain for himself.

sentences.zh: 遇大水，百方拯恤，民忘其困。

translations.literal: When great floods came, he exhausted every means to rescue and relieve the people, who forgot their distress.
translations.idiomatic: When catastrophic floods struck, he tried every means to rescue and relieve the people, who came to forget their hardship under his care.

sentences.zh: 織造中官李實素貪橫，妄增定額，恣誅求。

translations.literal: The weaving commissioner eunuch Li Shi had always been greedy and overbearing, arbitrarily increasing the fixed quotas and extorting at will.
translations.idiomatic: The weaving commissioner eunuch Li Shi had long been greedy and tyrannical, arbitrarily raising fixed quotas and extorting at will.

sentences.zh: 蘇州同知楊姜署府事，實惡其不屈，摭他事劾之。

translations.literal: Yang Jiang, vice prefect of Suzhou, was acting prefect; Shi hated his refusal to submit and seized on other matters to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiang, vice prefect of Suzhou, was acting in the prefect's stead; Li Shi resented his refusal to yield and trumped up other charges to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 起元至，即為姜辨冤，且上去蠹七事，語多侵實。

translations.literal: When Qiyuan arrived, he immediately pleaded Yang Jiang's innocence and also submitted to the throne seven items on removing corruption, many of whose words impinged on Shi.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Qiyuan arrived, he pleaded Yang Jiang's innocence and also submitted to the throne seven proposals for rooting out corruption, many of which struck directly at Li Shi.

sentences.zh: 實欲姜行屬吏禮，再疏誣逮之。

translations.literal: Shi wanted Jiang to perform the rites due a subordinate official; he submitted a second memorial with false charges to have him arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi wanted Yang Jiang to observe the ceremonial deference owed a subordinate official and submitted a second memorial with false charges to have him arrested.

sentences.zh: 起元再疏雪姜，更切直。

translations.literal: Qiyuan submitted a second memorial to clear Jiang, even more blunt and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan submitted a second memorial to clear Yang Jiang's name, even more blunt and uncompromising than before.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢庇實，取嚴旨責起元，令速上姜貪劣狀。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian shielded Shi and obtained a stern edict rebuking Qiyuan, ordering him to submit promptly a report on Jiang's greed and misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian shielded Li Shi and procured a stern edict rebuking Qiyuan, ordering him to submit at once a report on Yang Jiang's greed and misconduct.

sentences.zh: 起元益頌姜廉謹，詆實誣毀，因引罪乞罷。

translations.literal: Qiyuan all the more praised Jiang's integrity and prudence, denounced Shi's slander, and on that account submitted his own guilt and begged to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan praised Yang Jiang's integrity and prudence all the more strongly, denounced Li Shi's slanderous charges, and submitted his own resignation in protest.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大怒，矯旨斥姜為民。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly angered and forged an edict dismissing Jiang to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was furious and forged an edict stripping Yang Jiang of office and reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 起元復劾實貪恣不法數事，而為姜求寬。

translations.literal: Qiyuan again impeached Shi for several acts of greed, arrogance, and lawlessness, while pleading for leniency toward Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan again impeached Li Shi on several counts of greed, arrogance, and lawlessness, while pleading for leniency toward Yang Jiang.

sentences.zh: 實以此斂威，而忠賢遂銜起元不置。

translations.literal: Shi thereby reined in his arrogance somewhat, but Zhongxian henceforth bore an implacable grudge against Qiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi moderated his arrogance somewhat as a result, but Zhongxian henceforth nursed an implacable grudge against Qiyuan.

sentences.zh: 分守參政朱童蒙者，先為兵科都給事中，以攻鄒元標講學外遷，失誌狂暴，每行道輒鞭撲數十人，血肉狼籍。

translations.literal: The guarding administration commissioner Zhu Tongmeng had earlier served as chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of War; for attacking Zou Yuanbiao's lecturing he was transferred outward, lost his ambition, and became violent; whenever he went on the road he would whip and beat dozens of people, leaving flesh and blood strewn about.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tongmeng, the guarding administration commissioner, had earlier served as chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of War; after he was posted out of the capital for attacking Zou Yuanbiao's lecturing activities, he lost his bearings and turned savage, whipping and beating dozens of people whenever he traveled, leaving the roads strewn with blood.

sentences.zh: 起元欲糾之，童蒙遂稱病去，起元乃列其貪虐狀以聞。

translations.literal: When Qiyuan wished to impeach him, Tongmeng then claimed illness and left; Qiyuan thereupon listed his greedy and tyrannical conduct and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiyuan moved to impeach him, Tongmeng claimed illness and left his post; Qiyuan then submitted a detailed report of his greed and cruelty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 忠賢遂矯旨削起元籍，擢童蒙京卿。

translations.literal: Zhongxian then forged an edict stripping Qiyuan of his registry and promoting Tongmeng to a capital ministerial post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian then forged an edict stripping Qiyuan of his official registry and promoting Tongmeng to a capital ministerial post.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，忠賢欲殺高攀龍、周順昌、繆昌期、黃尊素、李應升、周宗建六人，取實空印疏，令其黨李永貞、李朝欽誣起元為巡撫時乾沒帑金十余萬，日與攀龍輩往來講學，因行居間。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, Zhongxian wished to kill Gao Panlong, Zhou Shunchang, Miao Changqi, Huang Zunsu, Li Yingsheng, and Zhou Zongjian—the six men—and took Shi's memorial on blank seals, ordering his partisans Li Yongzhen and Li Chaoqin to falsely charge that while grand coordinator Qiyuan had embezzled more than a hundred thousand taels from the treasury, he daily associated with Panlong and the others in lecturing and acted as go-between.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year, Zhongxian set out to kill Gao Panlong, Zhou Shunchang, Miao Changqi, Huang Zunsu, Li Yingsheng, and Zhou Zongjian. He seized on Li Shi's memorial concerning blank official seals and had his partisans Li Yongzhen and Li Chaoqin fabricate charges that Qiyuan, while serving as grand coordinator, had embezzled more than a hundred thousand taels from the treasury, met daily with Panlong and the others for scholarly gatherings, and acted as their go-between.

sentences.zh: 矯旨逮起元，至則順昌等已斃獄中。

translations.literal: A forged edict arrested Qiyuan; when he arrived, Shunchang and the others had already died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: A forged edict ordered Qiyuan's arrest; by the time he reached the capital, Shunchang and the others had already perished in prison.

sentences.zh: 許顯純酷榜掠，竟如實疏，懸贓十萬。

translations.literal: Xu Xianchun cruelly tortured him under the rod; in the end it matched Shi's memorial, and a fine of a hundred thousand taels in illicit gains was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianchun tortured him brutally under interrogation until the confession matched Li Shi's memorial, and a fine of a hundred thousand taels in illicit gains was imposed.

sentences.zh: 罄貲不足，親故多破其家。

translations.literal: When all his property was exhausted it was still not enough, and many relatives and friends were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Even when his entire estate was liquidated the sum could not be met, and many relatives and friends were ruined in the effort.

sentences.zh: 九月斃之獄中，吳士民及其鄉人無不垂涕者。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was beaten to death in prison; among the gentry and common people of Wu and his fellow townsmen there was none who did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was beaten to death in prison; among the gentry and common people of the Wu region and his fellow townsmen, there was scarcely one who did not weep.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，贈兵部右侍郎，官一子。

translations.literal: When the Zhuanglie Emperor succeeded to the throne, Qiyuan was posthumously granted the post of right vice minister of war, and one son was given an official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, Qiyuan was posthumously granted the rank of right vice minister of war, and one son was given an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚忠惠。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, he was posthumously given the temple name Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted the posthumous title Loyal and Kind.

sentences.zh: 繆昌期，字當時，江陰人。

translations.literal: Miao Changqi, styled Dangshi, was a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Changqi, styled Dangshi, was a native of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 為諸生有盛名，舉萬歷四十一年進士，改庶吉士，年五十有二矣。

translations.literal: As a student he enjoyed great renown; in the forty-first year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination, was changed to a Hanlin bachelor, and was already fifty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: As a licentiate he enjoyed great renown; in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor, by which time he was already fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 有同年生忌之，揚言為於玉立所薦，自是有東林之目。

translations.literal: A fellow graduate who envied him spread word that he had been recommended by Yu Yuli, and from then on he bore the label of the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow graduate who envied him spread word that he had been recommended by Yu Yuli, and from that point he was marked as a Donglin man.

sentences.zh: 張差梃擊事，劉廷元倡言瘋癲，劉光復和之，疏詆發訐者，謂不當詫之為奇貨，居之為元功。

translations.literal: In the Zhang Chai club-attack affair, Liu Tingyuan took the lead in calling it madness, Liu Guangfu echoed him, and in a memorial they slandered those who exposed the plot, saying one ought not treat it as a rare prize or claim it as a supreme achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhang Chai club-attack affair, Liu Tingyuan took the lead in calling the assailant mad, Liu Guangfu echoed him, and in a memorial they vilified those who had exposed the plot, arguing that the incident ought not be treated as a political prize or claimed as a supreme achievement.

sentences.zh: 昌期憤，語朝士曰：「奸徒狙擊青宮，此何等事，乃以『瘋癲』二字庇天下亂臣賊子，以『奇貨元功』四字沒天下忠臣義士哉！」

translations.literal: Changqi was indignant and said to court officials: "Villains lay in ambush to strike at the Eastern Palace—what sort of affair is this, that with the two words 'madness' you would shield all the rebellious ministers and traitorous sons under heaven, and with the four words 'rare prize, supreme achievement' you would bury all the loyal ministers and righteous men under heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Changqi was incensed and said to his colleagues at court: "Villains lay in wait to strike at the heir apparent—what manner of crime is this, that with the word 'madness' you would shield every rebel and traitor in the realm, and with the phrase 'rare prize, supreme achievement' you would bury every loyal and righteous man!

sentences.zh: 廷元輩聞其語，深疾之。

translations.literal: When Tingyuan and his party heard his words, they deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingyuan and his allies heard these words, they came to hate him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉文炳劾大學士吳道南，遂陰詆昌期。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Wenbing impeached Grand Secretary Wu Daonan and thereupon secretly slandered Changqi.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Wenbing impeached Grand Secretary Wu Daonan and took the opportunity to slander Changqi in secret.

sentences.zh: 時方授檢討，文炳再疏顯攻，昌期即移疾去。

translations.literal: At the time he had just been appointed revising compiler; Wenbing submitted a second memorial openly attacking him, and Changqi immediately submitted notice of illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he had just been appointed revising compiler; Wenbing submitted a second memorial openly attacking him, and Changqi promptly submitted notice of illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 既而京察，廷元輩復思中之，學士劉一燝力持乃免。

translations.literal: Later, at the capital evaluation, Tingyuan's party again thought to strike him down, but Bachelor Liu Yijin forcefully upheld him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the capital evaluation of officials, Tingyuan's faction again tried to bring him down, but Bachelor Liu Yijin forcefully intervened and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年還朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianqi reign he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 一燝以次輔當國。

translations.literal: Yijin was secondary grand secretary and held state power.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijin was serving as secondary grand secretary and directing affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 其冬，首輔葉向高至。

translations.literal: That winter, chief grand secretary Ye Xianggao arrived.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Chief Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 小人間一燝於向高，謂欲沮其來，向高不悅。

translations.literal: Petty men sowed discord between Yijin and Xianggao, saying that Yijin wished to obstruct his coming; Xianggao was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men sowed discord between Yijin and Xianggao, claiming that Yijin wished to obstruct his arrival; Xianggao was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會給事中孫傑承魏忠賢指，劾一燝及周嘉謨，忠賢遽傳旨允放。

translations.literal: It happened that Supervising Secretary Sun Jie, acting on Wei Zhongxian's direction, impeached Yijin and Zhou Jiamo; Zhongxian promptly transmitted an edict approving their dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: At that point Supervising Secretary Sun Jie, acting on Wei Zhongxian's instructions, impeached Yijin and Zhou Jiamo, and Zhongxian promptly transmitted an edict approving their dismissal.

sentences.zh: 昌期急詣向高，力言二人顧命重臣，不可輕逐，內傳不可奉。

translations.literal: Changqi hurried to see Xianggao and forcefully argued that the two men were heavy ministers entrusted at the deathbed and must not be lightly expelled, and that edicts transmitted from within must not be obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi hurried to see Xianggao and argued forcefully that the two men were weighty ministers entrusted at the deathbed and must not be dismissed lightly, and that edicts transmitted from within the palace must not simply be obeyed.

sentences.zh: 向高怫然曰：「上所傳，何敢不奉？」

translations.literal: Xianggao said displeased: "What the sovereign transmits—how dare one not obey?
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said, displeased, "What the sovereign transmits—how dare we refuse to obey?

sentences.zh: 昌期曰：「公，三朝老臣。

translations.literal: Changqi said: "Your Excellency is an elder minister of three reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi replied, "Your Excellency is an elder statesman who has served three reigns.

sentences.zh: 始至之日，以去就力爭，必可得也。

translations.literal: On the very day you arrive, if you struggle over staying or leaving with all your force, you are sure to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: On the very day you take office, if you stake your own position on this fight, you are sure to prevail.

sentences.zh: 若一傳而放兩大臣，異日天子手滑，不復可止矣。」

translations.literal: If at one transmission two great ministers are dismissed, another day when the Son of Heaven's hand slips, it will no longer be possible to stop."
translations.idiomatic: If at a single transmitted edict two great ministers are dismissed, then another day when the emperor's hand slips, there will be no stopping it."

sentences.zh: 向高默然。

translations.literal: Xianggao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao fell silent.

sentences.zh: 昌期因備言一燝質直無他腸，向高意少解。

translations.literal: Changqi thereupon fully explained that Yijin was honest and straightforward without other designs, and Xianggao's mind was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi then explained at length that Yijin was honest and straightforward and harbored no hidden designs, and Xianggao's mind was somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 會顧大章亦為向高言之，一燝乃得善去。

translations.literal: It happened that Gu Dazhang also spoke to Xianggao on his behalf, and Yijin was thus able to leave office honorably.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Dazhang also spoke to Xianggao on Yijin's behalf, and Yijin was thus able to leave office with honor intact.

sentences.zh: 兩人故向高門下士也。

translations.literal: Both men had formerly been disciples under Xianggao's patronage.
translations.idiomatic: Both men had formerly been protégés in Xianggao's circle.

sentences.zh: 昌期尋遷左贊善，進諭德。

translations.literal: Changqi was soon transferred to left tutor in the heir apparent's establishment and advanced to preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi was soon promoted to left tutor in the heir apparent's establishment and then to preceptor.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾忠賢疏上，昌期適過向高。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian's memorial impeaching Zhongxian was submitted, Changqi happened to be visiting Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian's memorial impeaching Zhongxian was submitted, Changqi happened to be visiting Xianggao.

sentences.zh: 向高曰：「楊君此疏太率易。

translations.literal: Xianggao said: "Master Yang's memorial is too rash.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said, "Master Yang's memorial is far too rash.

sentences.zh: 其人於上前時有匡正。

translations.literal: This man at times before the sovereign has offered correction.
translations.idiomatic: The man has at times offered the emperor sound correction.

sentences.zh: 鳥飛入宮，上乘梯手攫之，其人挽衣不得上。

translations.literal: A bird flew into the palace; the sovereign climbed a ladder and tried to seize it with his hand, and the man held his robe so he could not climb up.
translations.idiomatic: Once a bird flew into the palace; the emperor climbed a ladder to seize it by hand, and the man held his robe so that he could not climb up.

sentences.zh: 有小珰賜緋者，叱曰：『此非汝分，雖賜不得衣也。』

translations.literal: When a minor eunuch was granted crimson robes, he rebuked him, saying: 'This is not your station; even if granted, you may not wear it.'
translations.idiomatic: When a junior eunuch was granted crimson robes, he rebuked him, saying, 'That rank is not yours; even if it is granted, you may not wear it.'

sentences.zh: 其強直如此。

translations.literal: Such was his forceful uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his forceful uprightness.

sentences.zh: 是疏行，安得此小心謹慎之人在上左右？」

translations.literal: If this memorial goes forward, how can such a careful and prudent man remain at the sovereign's side?
translations.idiomatic: If this memorial goes forward, how can such a careful and prudent man remain at the emperor's side?

sentences.zh: 昌期愕然曰：「誰為此言以誤公？

translations.literal: Changqi said in astonishment: "Who spoke such words to mislead Your Excellency?
translations.idiomatic: Changqi said in astonishment, "Who told you such things and led you astray?

sentences.zh: 可斬也。」

translations.literal: He deserves execution."
translations.idiomatic: That person deserves execution."

sentences.zh: 向高色變，昌期徐起去。

translations.literal: Xianggao's countenance changed; Changqi slowly rose and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao's expression changed; Changqi rose slowly and took his leave.

sentences.zh: 語聞於漣，漣怒。

translations.literal: The words reached Lian, and Lian was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Word of this reached Yang Lian, who was furious.

sentences.zh: 向高亦內慚，密具揭，請帝允忠賢辭，忠賢大慍。

translations.literal: Xianggao also felt inward shame; he secretly prepared a memorial asking the emperor to accept Zhongxian's resignation, and Zhongxian was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao was inwardly ashamed as well; he secretly prepared a memorial asking the emperor to accept Zhongxian's resignation, and Zhongxian was furious.

sentences.zh: 會有言漣疏乃昌期代草者，忠賢遂深怒不可解。

translations.literal: It happened that there was talk that Lian's memorial had been drafted for him by Changqi; Zhongxian's deep anger then became irreconcilable.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then spread that Yang Lian's memorial had been drafted by Changqi, and Zhongxian's rage became irreconcilable.

sentences.zh: 及向高去，韓爌秉政，忠賢逐趙南星、高攀龍、魏大中及漣、光鬥，爌皆具揭懇留。

translations.literal: When Xianggao left office, Han Kuang held power; Zhongxian expelled Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Wei Dazhong, and Lian and Guangdou; Kuang each time submitted memorials earnestly asking them to be retained.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianggao left office, Han Kuang took charge of government; Zhongxian drove out Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, Wei Dazhong, and Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou, and each time Kuang submitted earnest memorials asking that they be retained.

sentences.zh: 忠賢及其黨謂昌期實左右之。

translations.literal: Zhongxian and his party said that Changqi was really the one steering him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian and his faction claimed that Changqi was really pulling the strings behind Kuang.

sentences.zh: 而昌期於諸人去國，率送之郊外，執手太息，由是忠賢益恨。

translations.literal: Yet whenever these men left the state, Changqi would as a rule escort them to the suburbs, take their hands, and sigh deeply; because of this Zhongxian hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever these men were driven from office, Changqi would as a rule escort them to the suburbs, take their hands, and sigh deeply; Zhongxian hated him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 昌期知勢不可留，具疏乞假，遂落職閑住。

translations.literal: Changqi knew the situation could not be sustained and submitted a memorial begging leave; he then lost his post and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi saw that the situation could not be sustained, submitted a memorial requesting leave, and was stripped of office to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 五年春，以汪文言獄詞連及，削職提問。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, he was implicated through the testimony in the Wang Wenyan case, stripped of office, and summoned for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he was implicated through testimony in the Wang Wenyan case, stripped of office, and summoned for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 忠賢恨不置。

translations.literal: Zhongxian's hatred knew no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian's hatred knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 明年二月復於他疏責昌期已削籍猶冠蓋延賓，令緹騎逮問。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, again in another memorial he rebuked Changqi for, though already stripped of registry, still keeping official carriage and canopy and receiving guests, and ordered the imperial guards to arrest and interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, in yet another memorial he rebuked Changqi for, though already stripped of his registry, still keeping official carriage and receiving guests, and ordered the imperial guards to arrest and interrogate him.

sentences.zh: 逾月，復入之李實疏中，下詔獄。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he was again implicated in Li Shi's memorial and sent to the imperial prison by secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was once more named in a memorial by Li Shi and thrown into the secret prison on imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 昌期慷慨對簿，詞氣不撓，竟坐贓三千，五毒備至。

translations.literal: Changqi answered boldly at trial, his words and bearing unyielding; in the end he was convicted of embezzling three thousand taels, and the full array of the five tortures was applied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi faced interrogation with fierce courage, his tone never breaking; he was ultimately found guilty of three thousand taels in graft and subjected to every form of the five tortures.

sentences.zh: 四月晦，斃於獄。

translations.literal: On the last day of the fourth month, he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: On the final day of the fourth month he perished in jail.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，贈詹事兼侍讀學士，錄其一子，詔並予謚。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, [Changqi] was posthumously made Grand Mentor and concurrent Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting, one of his sons was granted office, and an edict also conferred a posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chongzhen Emperor took the throne, Changqi was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, one son was given an official appointment, and an edict granted him a posthumous title as well.

sentences.zh: 而是時，姚希孟以詞臣持物論，雅不善左光鬥、周宗建，力尼之，遂並昌期及周起元、李應升、黃尊素、周朝瑞、袁化中、顧大章，皆不獲謚。

translations.literal: But at that time Yao Ximeng, as a literary official wielding public opinion, had never been on good terms with Zuo Guangdou and Zhou Zongjian and strenuously blocked it; thus Changqi, together with Zhou Qiyuan, Li Yingsheng, Huang Zunsu, Zhou Chaorui, Yuan Huazhong, and Gu Dazhang, all failed to receive posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yao Ximeng, a court writer who shaped public discourse, had long disliked Zuo Guangdou and Zhou Zongjian and fought hard to stop it—so neither Changqi nor Zhou Qiyuan, Li Yingsheng, Huang Zunsu, Zhou Chaorui, Yuan Huazhong, nor Gu Dazhang received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 福王時，始謚文貞。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, [he] was at last given the posthumous name Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the reign of the Prince of Fu was he finally granted the posthumous name Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 周順昌，字景文，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shunchang, courtesy name Jingwen, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shunchang, styled Jingwen, came from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the forty-first year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授福州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 捕治稅監高寀爪牙，不少貸。

translations.literal: He arrested and punished the minions of the tax commissioner Gao Chai, granting them no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He seized and prosecuted the agents of the tax intendant Gao Chai without the slightest mercy.

sentences.zh: 寀激民變，劫辱巡撫袁一驥，質其二子，並質副使呂純如。

translations.literal: Chai incited a popular uprising, seized and humiliated Grand Coordinator Yuan Yiji, held his two sons hostage, and also held Deputy Commissioner Lü Chunru hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chai provoked a riot among the people, seized and abused Grand Coordinator Yuan Yiji, took his two sons as hostages, and did the same to Vice Commissioner Lü Chunru.

sentences.zh: 或議以順昌代，順昌不可，純如以此銜順昌。

translations.literal: Some proposed that Shunchang replace [Lü]; Shunchang refused, and Lü Chunru therefore bore a grudge against Shunchang.
translations.idiomatic: Some suggested sending Shunchang in Lü's place, but Shunchang would not agree—and from that day Lü Chunru nursed a grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 擢吏部稽勛主事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Merit Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Merit Records.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，歷文選員外郎，署選事。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he served successively as vice director in the Bureau of Appointments and temporarily managed selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi period he rose through the Bureau of Appointments to vice director and for a time oversaw official selection.

sentences.zh: 力杜請寄，抑僥幸，清操爵然。

translations.literal: He vigorously blocked patronage requests and checked opportunism; his integrity stood conspicuously apart.
translations.idiomatic: He worked hard to shut down backdoor appointments and curb the lucky climbers, his moral conduct shining unmistakably above the rest.

sentences.zh: 乞假歸。

translations.literal: He requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 順昌為人剛方貞介，疾惡如仇。

translations.literal: Shunchang was by nature upright, principled, and incorruptibly strict; he hated wickedness as if it were a personal enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Shunchang was rigidly honest and unbending in character, hating evil with the passion of a sworn foe.

sentences.zh: 巡撫周起元忤魏忠賢削籍，順昌為文送之，指斥無所諱。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Zhou Qiyuan offended Wei Zhongxian and was struck from the registers, Shunchang wrote a piece to send him off, denouncing [Wei] without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Zhou Qiyuan crossed Wei Zhongxian and was removed from office, Shunchang wrote a farewell essay for him, condemning the eunuch with nothing held back.

sentences.zh: 魏大中被逮，道吳門，順昌出餞，與同臥起者三日，許以女聘大中孫。

translations.literal: When Wei Dazhong was arrested and passed through Wu Gate, Shunchang went out to see him off, shared bed and board with him for three days, and promised his daughter in marriage to Dazhong's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Dazhong was taken into custody and came through Wu Gate, Shunchang went out to bid him farewell, slept and ate at his side for three days, and pledged his daughter to Dazhong's grandson.

sentences.zh: 旂尉屢趣行，順昌瞋目曰：「若不知世間有不畏死男子耶？

translations.literal: The imperial guards repeatedly urged [Dazhong] to depart; Shunchang glared and said: "Do you not know that in this world there are men who do not fear death?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's runners kept pressing them to move on; Shunchang fixed them with a glare and said, "Don't you know this world holds men who are not afraid to die?

sentences.zh: 歸語忠賢，我故吏部郎周順昌也。」

translations.literal: Go back and tell Zhongxian: I am Zhou Shunchang, formerly a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Go tell Zhongxian for me—I am Zhou Shunchang, once a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 因戟手呼忠賢名，罵不絕口。

translations.literal: Then, pointing his finger, he called out Zhongxian's name and cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He thrust out his hand toward heaven, shouting Zhongxian's name and raining curses without pause.

sentences.zh: 旂尉歸，以告忠賢。

translations.literal: The imperial guards returned and reported this to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: The guards went back and told Zhongxian everything.

sentences.zh: 御史倪文煥者，忠賢義子也，誣劾同官夏之令，致之死。

translations.literal: Censor Ni Wenhuan was Zhongxian's adopted son; he falsely impeached his colleague Xia Zhiling and brought about his death.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Ni Wenhuan was Zhongxian's sworn son; he framed his fellow censor Xia Zhiling on false charges and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 順昌嘗語人，他日倪御史當償夏御史命。

translations.literal: Shunchang once told people: "One day Censor Ni will pay with his life for Censor Xia."
translations.idiomatic: Shunchang had once remarked to others, "The day will come when Censor Ni pays for Censor Xia's life."

sentences.zh: 文煥大恚，遂承忠賢指，劾順昌與罪人婚，且誣以贓賄，忠賢即矯旨削奪。

translations.literal: Wenhuan was greatly enraged; he then carried out Zhongxian's instructions, impeaching Shunchang for marrying his daughter to the family of a criminal and also falsely charging him with bribery and embezzlement, whereupon Zhongxian immediately forged an edict stripping him of rank and privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan flew into a rage, followed Zhongxian's lead, and impeached Shunchang for betrothing his daughter to a criminal's kin while also accusing him of graft; Zhongxian at once forged an edict to strip him of rank and honors.

sentences.zh: 先所忤副使呂純如，順昌同郡人，以京卿家居，挾前恨，數譖於織造中官李實及巡撫毛一鷺。

translations.literal: Lü Chunru, whom he had previously offended and who was a fellow townsman now living at home as a senior capital official, repeatedly slandered him to the eunuch commissioner Li Shi, supervisor of silk production, and Grand Coordinator Mao Yilu, bearing his old grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chunru—the vice commissioner Shunchang had crossed long before, a man of the same county now retired at home as a senior metropolitan official—nursed his old resentment and repeatedly denounced Shunchang to the weaving commissioner eunuch Li Shi and Grand Coordinator Mao Yilu.

sentences.zh: 已，實追論周起元，遂誣順昌請囑，有所乾沒，與起元等並逮。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Li Shi pursued charges against Zhou Qiyuan and then falsely accused Shunchang of soliciting favors and embezzling funds; Shunchang was arrested along with Qiyuan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Shi reopened the case against Zhou Qiyuan and then claimed Shunchang had solicited favors and skimmed money; Shunchang was arrested together with Qiyuan and the rest.

sentences.zh: 順昌好為德於鄉，有冤抑及郡中大利害，輒為所司陳說，以故士民德順昌甚。

translations.literal: Shunchang liked to do good for his home district; whenever there were cases of injustice or major public issues in the prefecture, he would plead them before the authorities, and for this reason scholars and commoners deeply esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shunchang was generous with his neighbors: whenever someone suffered wrongful treatment or the prefecture faced a matter of great public consequence, he would take the case to the proper officials—and for this the gentry and people loved him dearly.

sentences.zh: 及聞逮者至，眾鹹憤怒，號冤者塞道。

translations.literal: When word came that the arrest party had arrived, the crowd all grew furious, and those crying injustice filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: When news spread that the arresting officers were coming, the whole populace erupted in anger, and the streets filled with voices pleading innocence.

sentences.zh: 至開讀日，不期而集者數萬人，鹹執香為周吏部乞命。

translations.literal: On the day the warrant was to be read aloud, tens of thousands gathered unbidden, all holding incense and begging for the life of Former Minister Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the edict of arrest was to be read, tens of thousands assembled without being summoned, incense in hand, begging heaven for the life of the former minister Zhou.

sentences.zh: 諸生文震亨、楊廷樞、王節、劉羽翰等前謁一鷺及巡按御史徐吉，請以民情上聞。

translations.literal: The students Wen Zhenheng, Yang Tingji, Wang Jie, Liu Yuhan, and others went forward to call on Mao Yilu and touring censor Xu Ji, asking that public sentiment be reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Students Wen Zhenheng, Yang Tingji, Wang Jie, Liu Yuhan, and others came forward to petition Mao Yilu and touring censor Xu Ji, urging them to relay the people's feelings to the throne.

sentences.zh: 旗尉厲聲罵曰：「東廠逮人，鼠輩敢爾！」

translations.literal: The flag guards shouted curses: "The Eastern Depot is making an arrest—you vermin dare behave like this!
translations.idiomatic: A flag guard snarled, "The Eastern Depot has come to take a man—how dare you rats act this way!

sentences.zh: 大呼：「囚安在？」

translations.literal: They bellowed: "Where is the prisoner?"
translations.idiomatic: He roared, "Where is the prisoner?"

sentences.zh: 手擲鋃鐺於地，聲瑯然。

translations.literal: They threw manacles to the ground with a clang.
translations.idiomatic: He hurled shackles to the ground with a ringing crash.

sentences.zh: 眾益憤，曰：「始吾以為天子命，乃東廠耶！」

translations.literal: The crowd grew even angrier and said: "At first we thought this was the Son of Heaven's command—so it is the Eastern Depot after all!
translations.idiomatic: The people grew still more furious and cried, "We thought this was the Son of Heaven's order—so it is the Eastern Depot!

sentences.zh: 蜂擁大呼，勢如山崩。

translations.literal: They surged forward with a great roar, their momentum like an avalanche.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed in with a thunderous shout, their force like a collapsing mountain.

sentences.zh: 旂尉東西竄，眾縱橫毆擊，斃一人，余負重傷，逾垣走。

translations.literal: The flag guards fled in all directions; the crowd beat them at will, killing one man, leaving the rest badly wounded to scale walls and flee.
translations.idiomatic: The guards scattered in every direction as the mob fell upon them; one was beaten to death, the others left grievously wounded and fled over the walls.

sentences.zh: 一鷺、吉不能語。

translations.literal: Mao Yilu and Xu Ji were speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yilu and Xu Ji could not utter a word.

sentences.zh: 知府寇慎、知縣陳文瑞素得民，曲為解諭，眾始散。

translations.literal: Prefect Kou Shen and Magistrate Chen Wenrui, who had long enjoyed the people's trust, gently reasoned with them, and only then did the crowd disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Kou Shen and Magistrate Chen Wenrui, both men the people had long trusted, spoke to them with patience and tact, and at last the crowd broke up.

sentences.zh: 順昌乃自詣吏。

translations.literal: Shunchang then presented himself to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shunchang then went of his own accord to surrender to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 又三日北行，一鷺飛章告變，東廠刺事者言吳人盡反，謀斷水道，劫漕舟，忠賢大懼。

translations.literal: Three days later, as he traveled north, Mao Yilu sent an urgent memorial reporting a rebellion; Eastern Depot informants said the people of Wu had all risen, plotting to cut the waterways and seize grain-transport boats, and Zhongxian was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, as Shunchang was escorted north, Mao Yilu fired off an urgent report of insurrection; Eastern Depot spies claimed all Wu had revolted and planned to block the canals and seize the grain barges—and Zhongxian was terrified.

sentences.zh: 已而一鷺言縛得倡亂者顏佩韋、馬傑、沈揚、楊念如、周文元等，亂已定，忠賢乃安。

translations.literal: Before long Mao Yilu reported that the ringleaders Yan Peiwei, Ma Jie, Shen Yang, Yang Nianru, Zhou Wenyuan, and others had been bound; once the disturbance was declared settled, Zhongxian calmed down.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mao Yilu wrote that the instigators Yan Peiwei, Ma Jie, Shen Yang, Yang Nianru, Zhou Wenyuan, and others had been captured; with the trouble declared over, Zhongxian finally eased his mind.

sentences.zh: 然自是緹騎不出國門矣。

translations.literal: From then on, however, imperial arrest parties no longer ventured beyond the capital gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from that time forward the emperor's arrest squads never again dared leave the capital.

sentences.zh: 順昌至京師，下詔獄。

translations.literal: When Shunchang reached the capital, he was sent to the imperial prison by secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the capital, Shunchang was consigned to the secret prison by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 許顯純鍛煉，坐贓三千，五日一酷掠，每掠治，必大罵忠賢。

translations.literal: Xu Xianchun fabricated his confession; he was convicted of embezzling three thousand taels; every five days he was savagely tortured, and at each session he invariably cursed Zhongxian loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianchun tortured a confession out of him and fixed his guilt at three thousand taels in stolen funds; every five days came a brutal round of beating, and each time Shunchang would hurl abuse at Zhongxian with all his might.

sentences.zh: 顯純椎落其齒，自起問曰：「復能罵魏上公否？」

translations.literal: Xu Xianchun knocked out his teeth with a mallet, rose himself, and asked: "Can you still curse Grand Duke Wei?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianchun smashed out his teeth with a club, stood up, and demanded, "Can you still curse the Grand Duke Wei?

sentences.zh: 順昌噀血唾其面，罵益厲。

translations.literal: Shunchang spat blood in his face and cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Shunchang sprayed blood and spittle into his face and cursed him all the harder.

sentences.zh: 遂於夜中潛斃之。

translations.literal: He was then secretly killed in the night.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was quietly murdered in his cell.

sentences.zh: 時六年六月十有七日也。

translations.literal: It was the seventeenth day of the sixth month of the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: The date was the seventeenth day of the sixth month in the sixth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 明年，莊烈帝即位，文煥伏誅，實下吏，一鷺、吉坐建忠賢祠，純如坐頌珰，並麗逆案。

translations.literal: The following year the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne; Wenhuan was executed, Shi was handed to the authorities, Mao Yilu and Xu Ji were implicated for building temples to Zhongxian, and Lü Chunru for praising the eunuch faction—all were charged in the treason cases.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Chongzhen Emperor took the throne, Wenhuan was put to death, Li Shi was arrested, Mao Yilu and Xu Ji were condemned for erecting shrines to Zhongxian, and Lü Chunru for lauding the eunuch clique—all swept into the roll of traitors.

sentences.zh: 順昌贈太常卿，官其一子。

translations.literal: Shunchang was posthumously made Grand Master of Ceremonies, and one of his sons was granted an official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Shunchang was posthumously elevated to Grand Master of Ceremonies, and one son received an official post.

sentences.zh: 給事中瞿式耜訟諸臣冤，稱順昌及楊漣、魏大中清忠尤著，詔謚忠介。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Qu Shisi petitioned on the wronged ministers' behalf, declaring that Shunchang along with Yang Lian and Wei Dazhong were outstanding in purity and loyalty; an edict conferred the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Qu Shisi appealed for the wronged officials, praising Shunchang together with Yang Lian and Wei Dazhong as paragons of loyal integrity; the throne granted Shunchang the posthumous name Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 長子茂蘭，字子佩，刺血書疏，詣闕訴冤，詔以所贈官推及其祖父。

translations.literal: His eldest son Maolan, courtesy name Zipei, wrote a memorial in his own blood, went to the capital to plead the injustice, and an edict extended the conferred rank to his grandfather as well.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Maolan, styled Zipei, pricked his finger and wrote a memorial in blood, then went to court to plead his father's case; an edict extended the posthumous honors to his grandfather as well.

sentences.zh: 茂蘭更上疏，請給三世誥命，建祠賜額。

translations.literal: Maolan submitted another memorial requesting grand edicts for three generations, the building of a shrine, and an inscribed plaque.
translations.idiomatic: Maolan memorialized again, asking for patent letters of honor for three generations, a commemorative shrine, and an imperial inscription.

sentences.zh: 帝悉報可，且命先後慘死諸臣，鹹視此例。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved all of it and ordered that the other ministers who had died horribly be treated by the same precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted every request and commanded that the other officials who had died in similar agony be honored by the same standard.

sentences.zh: 茂蘭好學砥行，不就蔭敘。

translations.literal: Maolan loved learning and cultivated his conduct, refusing to take office through hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Maolan devoted himself to study and upright living, and would not accept appointment through inherited privilege.

sentences.zh: 國變後，隱居不出，以壽終。

translations.literal: After the dynastic catastrophe, he lived in seclusion and never emerged, dying of old age.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he withdrew from the world and never came forth again, living out his years in peace.

sentences.zh: 諸生朱祖文者，都督先之孫。

translations.literal: The student Zhu Zuwén was the grandson of Commander-in-Chief Zhu Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Among the students was Zhu Zuwen, grandson of the regional commander Zhu Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 當順昌被逮，間行詣都，為納饘粥、湯藥。

translations.literal: When Shunchang was arrested, he traveled secretly to the capital to provide gruel and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunchang was taken, Zhu Zuwen stole his way to the capital to bring him porridge and medicine.

sentences.zh: 及征贓令急，奔走稱貸諸公間。

translations.literal: When the order to collect the confiscated funds grew urgent, he hurried about borrowing money from various gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: When the demand for payment of the falsely assessed bribes turned fierce, he ran from one patron to another begging loans on Shunchang's behalf.

sentences.zh: 順昌櫬歸，祖文哀慟發病死。

translations.literal: When Shunchang's coffin returned, Zuwén grieved so deeply that he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunchang's coffin came home, Zuwen mourned himself into sickness and died.

sentences.zh: 佩韋等皆市人，文元則順昌輿隸也，論大辟。

translations.literal: Peiwei and the others were townspeople; Wenyuan was Shunchang's sedan-chair bearer—all were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Peiwei and his companions were common tradesmen; Wenyuan had been Shunchang's chair bearer—all received the death sentence.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，五人延頸就刃，語寇慎曰：「公好官，知我等好義，非亂也。」

translations.literal: Facing execution, the five stretched their necks to the blade and said to Kou Shen: "You are a good official; you know we acted from righteousness, not rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the block the five men offered their necks willingly and told Kou Shen, "You are an honest magistrate—you know we acted from loyalty, not rebellion.

sentences.zh: 監司張孝流涕而斬之。

translations.literal: Supervising official Zhang Xiao wept as he beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising official Zhang Xiao, weeping, carried out the execution.

sentences.zh: 吳人感其義，合葬之虎丘傍，題曰：「五人之墓」。

translations.literal: The people of Wu were moved by their righteousness and buried them together beside Tiger Hill, inscribing the tomb "Grave of the Five Men."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu, honoring their sacrifice, buried them together near Tiger Hill under the inscription "Tomb of the Five Men."

sentences.zh: 其地即一鷺所建忠賢普惠祠址也。

translations.literal: The site was precisely where Mao Yilu had built the Puhui Temple to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: That very ground was where Mao Yilu had erected his temple to Zhongxian, called Puhui.

sentences.zh: 周宗建，字季侯，吳江人，尚書用曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhou Zongjian, courtesy name Jihou, was a native of Wujiang and the great-grandson of Minister Zhou Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zongjian, styled Jihou, came from Wujiang and was the great-grandson of the minister Zhou Yong.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 除武康知縣，調繁仁和，有異政，入為御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Wukang, transferred to the busy district of Renhe where he achieved notable governance, then entered the capital as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served first as magistrate of Wukang, then was moved to the demanding county of Renhe, where his administration won notice; afterward he entered the capital as a censor.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，為顧存仁、王世貞、陶望齡、顧憲成請謚，追論萬歷朝小人，歷數錢夢臯、康丕揚、亓詩教、趙興邦亂政罪，並詆李三才、王圖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he petitioned for posthumous names for Gu Cunren, Wang Shizhen, Tao Wangling, and Gu Xiancheng, revisiting the petty men of the Wanli reign and enumerating the crimes of Qian Menggao, Kang Piyang, Qi Shijiao, and Zhao Xingbang in ruining government, while also denouncing Li Sancai and Wang Tu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he memorialized for posthumous honors for Gu Cunren, Wang Shizhen, Tao Wangling, and Gu Xiancheng, rehearsed the misdeeds of Wanli's small men, itemized the corrupt rule of Qian Menggao, Kang Piyang, Qi Shijiao, and Zhao Xingbang, and assailed Li Sancai and Wang Tu as well.

sentences.zh: 時遼事方棘，上疏責備輔臣。

translations.literal: The Liaodong crisis was then acute; he memorialized blaming the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: With the Liaodong emergency at its height, he submitted a memorial reproaching the grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 無何，沈陽破，宗建責當事大臣益急，因請破格用人，召還熊廷弼。

translations.literal: Before long Shenyang fell; Zongjian pressed the responsible ministers even harder, urging exceptional appointments and the recall of Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Shenyang fell; Zongjian pressed the ministers in charge ever more sharply, calling for bold appointments outside the usual channels and the recall of Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 已，論兵部尚書崔景榮不當信奸人劉保，輔臣劉一燝不當抑言路，因刺右通政林材、光祿卿李本固。

translations.literal: He then argued that War Minister Cui Jingrong ought not to have trusted the villain Liu Bao and that Chief Minister Liu Yiqian ought not to have suppressed the remonstrating officials, indirectly implicating Vice Commissioner of the Right Lin Cai and Chamberlain of Imperial Ceremonial Li Bengu.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to charge that War Minister Cui Jingrong should never have trusted the schemer Liu Bao, and that Grand Secretary Liu Yiqian should not have muzzled the censorial voice—aiming obliquely at Vice Commissioner Lin Cai and Chamberlain Li Bengu.

sentences.zh: 材、本固移疾去。

translations.literal: Lin and Li Bengu resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Cai and Li Bengu both pleaded illness and left office.

sentences.zh: 魏大中劾王德完庇楊鎬、李如楨，宗建為德完力攻大中，其持論數與東林左。

translations.literal: When Wei Dazhong impeached Wang Dewan for shielding Yang Hao and Li Ruzhen, Zongjian vigorously attacked Dazhong on Dewan's behalf; his positions often leaned against the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Dazhong impeached Wang Dewan for protecting Yang Hao and Li Ruzhen, Zongjian threw his weight behind Dewan and savaged Dazhong—his views repeatedly set him at odds with the Donglin party.

sentences.zh: 會是歲冬，奉聖夫人客氏既出宮復入，宗建首抗疏極諫，中言：「天子成言，有同兒戲。

translations.literal: That winter the Lady of Favor, the Nurse Ke, having left the palace was brought back in; Zongjian was first to submit a forceful remonstrance, saying among other things: "The Son of Heaven's settled word is treated like child's play.
translations.idiomatic: That same winter, after Nurse Ke—the Lady of Favor—had been sent from the palace and then recalled, Zongjian led the court in a fierce remonstrance, writing among other things: "The Son of Heaven's solemn word is tossed about like a child's game.

sentences.zh: 法宮禁地，僅類民家。

translations.literal: The sacred palace precinct is hardly different from a common household.
translations.idiomatic: The august inner palace has come to resemble an ordinary home.

sentences.zh: 聖朝舉動有乖，內外防閑盡廢。

translations.literal: The holy dynasty's conduct goes astray, and inner and outer barriers are wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The conduct of this sacred age has lost its way, and every safeguard between inner and outer court has been cast aside.

sentences.zh: 此輩一叨隆恩，便思逾分，狎溺無紀，漸成驕恣，釁孽日萌，後患難杜。

translations.literal: Once these people receive lofty favor, they at once aspire beyond their station, indulging themselves without restraint, gradually growing arrogant and willful; seeds of calamity sprout daily, and later troubles cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner do such people taste high favor than they reach beyond their rank, dissolving into unrestrained intimacy, swelling by degrees into arrogance and license; day by day the seeds of disaster take root, and the evils to come cannot be checked.

sentences.zh: 王聖、朱娥、陸令萱之覆轍，可為殷鑒。」

translations.literal: The overturned carts of Wang Sheng, Zhu E, and Lu Lingxuan should serve as bitter warnings.
translations.idiomatic: The ruined careers of Wang Sheng, Zhu E, and Lu Lingxuan stand before us as grim warnings.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，詰責。

translations.literal: The memorial offended the throne and drew rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran against the imperial will and brought down stern censure.

sentences.zh: 清議由此重之。

translations.literal: Public opinion therefore held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-minded opinion in the capital therefore esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 明年，廣寧失。

translations.literal: The next year Guangning was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Guangning fell.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多庇王化貞，欲甚熊廷弼罪。

translations.literal: Many court officials shielded Wang Huazhen and sought to magnify Xiong Tingbi's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Many at court rallied to Wang Huazhen's defense and tried to heap the greater blame on Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 宗建不平，為剖兩人罪案，頗右廷弼，諸庇化貞者乃深疾宗建。

translations.literal: Zongjian was indignant; he analyzed both men's cases and largely sided with Tingbi, so those protecting Huazhen came to deeply hate Zongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian would not have it; he laid out both men's records and largely vindicated Tingbi, and those who had shielded Huazhen thereafter hated Zongjian to the core.

sentences.zh: 京師久旱，五月雨雹。

translations.literal: The capital had long been dry; in the fifth month hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had suffered a long drought; in the fifth month hailstones fell.

sentences.zh: 宗建謂陰盛陽衰之征，歷陳四事：一專譏大學士沈纮；

translations.literal: Zongjian regarded this as a sign of yin prevailing and yang declining, and set forth four points: first, to criticize specifically Grand Secretary Shen Hong;
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian read this as a portent of yin overwhelming yang and laid out four grievances: first, a direct attack on Grand Secretary Shen Hong;

sentences.zh: 一請寬建言廢黜諸臣；

translations.literal: second, to ask leniency for the dismissed remonstrating officials;
translations.idiomatic: second, a plea to restore the officials dismissed for speaking out;

sentences.zh: 一言廷弼已有定案，不當因此羅織朝士，陰刺兵部尚書張鶴鳴、給事中郭鞏；

translations.literal: third, to say that since Xiong Tingbi's case was already settled, officials should not use it to entrap courtiers, obliquely attacking War Minister Zhang Heming and Supervising Secretary Guo Gong;
translations.idiomatic: third, the argument that Xiong Tingbi's case was already closed and must not be used to trap other courtiers—aimed covertly at War Minister Zhang Heming and Supervising Secretary Guo Gong;

sentences.zh: 一則專攻魏進忠，略言：「近日政事，外廷嘖嘖，鹹謂奧{穴交}之中，莫可測識，諭旨之下，有物憑焉。

translations.literal: fourth, to attack Wei Jinzhong specifically, saying in part: "Recently in state affairs the outer court murmurs that within the inner recesses of the palace nothing can be fathomed, and beneath issued edicts something lurks.
translations.idiomatic: and fourth, a direct assault on Wei Jinzhong, who wrote in part: "Lately in public affairs the outer court buzzes with complaint—all say that in the deep inner quarters of the palace nothing can be discerned, and that something stands behind every edict that comes down.

sentences.zh: 如魏進忠者，目不識一丁，而陛下假之嚬笑，日與相親。

translations.literal: Men like Wei Jinzhong cannot recognize a single character, yet Your Majesty grants him smiles and daily intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: A man like Wei Jinzhong cannot read a single character, yet Your Majesty shares smiles with him and keeps him close day after day.

sentences.zh: 一切用人行政，墮於其說，東西易向而不知，邪正顛倒而不覺。

translations.literal: All appointments and governance fall under his sway; east and west are reversed without awareness, wrong and right inverted without notice.
translations.idiomatic: Every appointment and every policy bends to his word; directions are swapped without your knowing it, and right and wrong stand on their heads while you remain unaware.

sentences.zh: 況內廷之借端，與外廷之投合，互相扶同。

translations.literal: Moreover the inner court finds pretexts while the outer court falls in line, each bolstering the other.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, the inner court seizes every excuse while the outer court falls into step—each side propping up the other.

sentences.zh: 離間之漸將起於蠅營，讒構之釁必生於長舌。

translations.literal: The first steps toward estrangement will arise from petty scheming; the breach of slander will surely spring from wagging tongues.
translations.idiomatic: The first rifts of division will begin with the buzzing of flies; the opening of calumny will surely come from long, loose tongues.

sentences.zh: 其為隱禍，可勝言哉！」

translations.literal: The hidden disasters this portends—can they even be fully spoken?
translations.idiomatic: The concealed calamities such conduct invites—who could exhaust them in words?

sentences.zh: 進忠者，魏忠賢故名也。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was Wei Zhongxian's original name.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong was the name Wei Zhongxian had borne before his rise.

sentences.zh: 時方結客氏為對食，廷臣多陰附之，其勢漸熾，見宗建疏，銜次骨，未發也。

translations.literal: At the time he had formed a paired household with Nurse Ke; many court officials secretly attached to him, his power steadily grew; reading Zongjian's memorial, he bore a grudge to the bone, though he had not yet acted.
translations.idiomatic: He was then living in a paired household with Nurse Ke; many officials quietly sided with him, and his power grew daily. When he read Zongjian's memorial he hated him to the marrow—but he had not yet struck.

sentences.zh: 鄒元標建首善書院，宗建實司其事。

translations.literal: Zou Yuanbiao founded the Shou Shan Academy; Zongjian in fact managed its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yuanbiao had established the Shou Shan Academy, and Zongjian in practice ran its affairs.

sentences.zh: 元標罷，宗建乞與俱罷，不從。

translations.literal: When Yuanbiao was dismissed, Zongjian asked to be dismissed with him, but the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanbiao was removed from office, Zongjian asked to resign with him, but the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 巡視光祿，與給事中羅尚忠力剔奸弊，節省為多。

translations.literal: He inspected the Grand Provisionerate and, together with Supervising Secretary Luo Shangzhong, vigorously rooted out corrupt abuses; savings were considerable.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the Grand Provisionerate, he worked with Supervising Secretary Luo Shangzhong to purge corruption aggressively, and the savings were substantial.

sentences.zh: 尋請核上供器物，中官怒，取旨詰責。

translations.literal: Soon he requested verification of tribute goods supplied to the court; the eunuchs were angered and obtained an edict rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon petitioned for an audit of imperial tribute goods. The eunuchs were furious and secured an edict denouncing him.

sentences.zh: 宗建等再疏力持，中人滋不悅。

translations.literal: Zongjian and others submitted further memorials steadfastly supporting him; the eunuchs grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian and others followed with further memorials in stout defense of him, and the eunuchs grew still more hostile.

sentences.zh: 給事中郭鞏者，先以劾廷弼被謫。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Guo Gong had earlier been demoted for impeaching Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Guo Gong had been demoted earlier for impeaching Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 廷弼敗，復官，遂深結進忠。

translations.literal: When Tingbi fell, he was restored to office and then formed deep ties with Jin Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Tingbi's downfall, Gong was restored to office and soon forged a close alliance with Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 知進忠最惡宗建，乃疏詆廷弼，因詆朝廷之薦廷弼者，而宗建與焉。

translations.literal: Knowing that Jin Zhong hated Zongjian above all, he memorialized slandering Tingbi and thereby slandering those at court who had recommended Tingbi, among whom was Zongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Wei Zhongxian loathed Zhou Zongjian above all others, Gong submitted a memorial vilifying Tingbi—and, by extension, everyone at court who had recommended him, Zongjian included.

sentences.zh: 其鋒銳甚，南京御史塗世業和之，詆宗建誤廷弼，且誤封疆。

translations.literal: His attack was very sharp; Nanjing Censor Tu Shiye chimed in, denouncing Zongjian for misleading Tingbi and thereby harming the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The assault was savagely pointed. Nanjing Censor Tu Shiye took it up, accusing Zongjian of having misled Tingbi and, in doing so, ruined the frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 宗建憤，疏駁世業，語侵鞏，抉其結納忠賢事。

translations.literal: Zongjian, furious, submitted a memorial refuting Shiye; his language impinged on Gong and exposed his collusion with the eunuch Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian, enraged, answered with a memorial rebutting Shiye. His language cut at Gong and laid bare Gong's collusion with the eunuch faction led by Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 鞏亦憤，上疏數千言，詆宗建益力，並及劉一燝、鄒元標、周嘉謨、楊漣、周朝瑞、毛士龍、方震孺、江秉謙、熊德陽輩數十人，悉指為廷弼逆黨。

translations.literal: Gong too was enraged and submitted a memorial of several thousand characters, attacking Zongjian all the more fiercely and naming dozens including Liu Yicheng, Zou Yuanbiao, Zhou Jiamou, Yang Lian, Zhou Chaorui, Mao Shilong, Fang Zhenru, Jiang Bingqian, and Xiong Deyang—calling them all partisans of the rebel Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, equally furious, submitted a memorial thousands of words long, redoubling his attack on Zongjian and dragging in dozens of men—Liu Yicheng, Zou Yuanbiao, Zhou Jiamou, Yang Lian, Zhou Chaorui, Mao Shilong, Fang Zhenru, Jiang Bingqian, Xiong Deyang, and others—branding them all traitorous partisans of Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 宗建益憤，抗疏力駁其謬，且曰：「李維翰、楊鎬、袁應泰、王化貞，皆壞封疆之人也；

translations.literal: Zongjian grew even angrier and submitted a defiant memorial vigorously refuting his falsehoods, saying: "Li Weihan, Yang Hao, Yuan Yingtai, and Wang Huazhen were all men who ruined the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian's fury only mounted. He submitted a defiant memorial forcefully dismantling the charges, writing: "Li Weihan, Yang Hao, Yuan Yingtai, and Wang Huazhen were all men who wrecked the frontier;

sentences.zh: 亓詩教力主催戰，趙興邦賄賣邊臣，皆誤封疆之人也；

translations.literal: Qi Shijiao forcefully urged premature battle, and Zhao Xingbang sold frontier posts through bribery—both were men who misled the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shijiao pressed relentlessly for rash campaigns, and Zhao Xingbang sold frontier appointments for bribes—both were men who misled the frontier;

sentences.zh: 其他薦維翰、薦鎬、薦應泰、化貞者，亦誤封疆之人也。

translations.literal: and those who recommended Weihan, Hao, Yingtai, and Huazhen were likewise men who misled the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: and every official who recommended Weihan, Hao, Yingtai, or Huazhen was likewise a man who misled the frontier.

sentences.zh: 鞏胡不一擊之，而獨苛求廷弼，且詆薦廷弼者為逆黨哉？」

translations.literal: Why does Gong not denounce them all, yet alone hound Tingbi and call those who recommended Tingbi traitors?
translations.idiomatic: Why does Gong not assail them all, yet singles out Tingbi for relentless attack and brands Tingbi's supporters as traitors?

sentences.zh: 當是時，忠賢勢益盛。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongxian's power was growing ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wei Zhongxian's power was waxing daily.

sentences.zh: 宗建慮內外合謀，其禍將大，三年二月遂抗疏直攻忠賢，略言：

translations.literal: Zongjian feared a convergence of intrigue inside and outside the palace and that disaster would be great; in the second month of the third year he submitted a defiant memorial directly attacking Zhongxian, stating in part:
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that inner and outer factions were closing ranks against him and that catastrophe was near, Zongjian in the second month of the third year submitted a defiant memorial aimed straight at Zhongxian, writing in part:

sentences.zh: 臣於去歲指名劾奏，進忠無一日忘臣。

translations.literal: Last year I named and impeached him in memorial; Jin Zhong has not forgotten me for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Last year I named Wei Zhongxian in a direct impeachment. He has not let a single day pass without remembering it.

sentences.zh: 於是乘私人郭鞏入都，嗾以傾臣，並傾諸異己者。

translations.literal: He has now taken advantage of my private enemy Guo Gong's arrival in the capital to incite him to overthrow me and overthrow all who differ from him.
translations.idiomatic: He has now seized on the arrival in the capital of my old enemy Guo Gong, goading him to bring me down—and with me, every man who stands apart from them.

sentences.zh: 鞏乃創為「新幽大幽」之說，把持察典，編廷臣數十人姓名為一冊，思一網中之。

translations.literal: Gong then invented the doctrine of 'New You and Great You,' seized control of the metropolitan examination, compiled the names of dozens of court officials into a register, and sought to snare them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Gong invented the doctrine of the 'Lesser Purge and Greater Purge,' took hold of the metropolitan examination, compiled the names of dozens of court officials into a single register, and plotted to sweep them all up in one net.

sentences.zh: 又為匿名書，羅織五十余人，投之道左，給事中則劉弘化為首，次及周朝瑞、熊德陽輩若而人，御史則方震孺為首，次及江秉謙輩若而人，而臣亦其中一人也。

translations.literal: He also composed an anonymous document fabricating charges against more than fifty people and cast it by the roadside; among supervising secretaries Liu Honghua was named first, followed by Zhou Chaorui, Xiong Deyang, and others; among censors Fang Zhenru was named first, followed by Jiang Bingqian and others—and I too was among them.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted an anonymous denunciation, fabricating charges against more than fifty men and leaving it by the roadside. Among the supervising secretaries, Liu Honghua was named first, then Zhou Chaorui, Xiong Deyang, and others; among the censors, Fang Zhenru led the list, followed by Jiang Bingqian and the rest—and my name appeared among them as well.

sentences.zh: 既欲羅諸臣，以快報復之私，更欲獨中臣，以釋進忠之恨。

translations.literal: He wished both to ensnare the officials to satisfy his private thirst for revenge, and to strike me alone in particular to vent Jin Zhong's hatred.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to entangle the whole corps of officials to satisfy a private hunger for revenge, yet strike me alone above all, to appease Wei Zhongxian's hatred.

sentences.zh: 是察典不出於朝廷，乃鞏及進忠之察典也。

translations.literal: This examination was not conducted by the court—it was Gong's and Jin Zhong's examination.
translations.idiomatic: This was no examination run by the court—it was an examination run by Gong and Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 幸直道在人，鞏說不行，始別借廷弼，欲一阱陷之。

translations.literal: Fortunately upright principle still had support among the people; Gong's scheme did not succeed, so he turned instead to using Tingbi as a pretext, intending to trap me in one fell swoop.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately, public regard for upright conduct still held, and Gong's scheme failed. He then seized on Tingbi as a fresh pretext, hoping to snare me in a single trap.

sentences.zh: 鞏又因臣論及王安，笑臣有何瓜葛。

translations.literal: Gong also, because I had mentioned Wang An in my memorial, mocked what connection I could possibly have with him.
translations.idiomatic: When my memorial touched on Wang An, Gong mocked me: what possible tie could I have to the man?

sentences.zh: 陛下亦知安之所以死乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty also know how An came to die?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty know how Wang An met his end?

sentences.zh: 身首異處，肉飽烏鳶，骨投黃犬，古今未有之慘也。

translations.literal: Body and head severed and cast apart, flesh left to gorge the crows and kites, bones thrown to yellow dogs—such cruelty is unmatched in history.
translations.idiomatic: Head and body hacked apart, flesh left for crows and kites to glut upon, bones fed to mangy dogs—a horror without precedent in all history.

sentences.zh: 鞏即心昵進忠，何至背公滅理，且牽連劉一燝、周嘉謨、楊漣、毛士龍輩，謂盡安黨。

translations.literal: Though Gong is close to Jin Zhong at heart, how could he betray the public good and abandon all principle, implicating Liu Yicheng, Zhou Jiamou, Yang Lian, Mao Shilong, and others by calling them all partisans of Wang An?
translations.idiomatic: Gong may be intimate with Wei Zhongxian in his heart, but how can he turn his back on the public good and cast aside all principle, dragging in Liu Yicheng, Zhou Jiamou, Yang Lian, Mao Shilong, and others as though they were all partisans of Wang An?

sentences.zh: 請陛下窮究安死果出何人傾害，則此事即進忠一大罪案。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to exhaustively investigate who truly engineered An's death—this matter alone would constitute a major crime of Jin Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to pursue to the end the question of who truly destroyed Wang An. That inquiry alone would expose one of Wei Zhongxian's gravest crimes.

sentences.zh: 鞏之媚進忠，即此可為證據矣。

translations.literal: That Gong fawns upon Jin Zhong may be seen as proof right here.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's sycophancy toward Wei Zhongxian is proof enough in itself.

sentences.zh: 先朝汪直、劉瑾，雖皆梟獍，幸言路清明，臣僚隔絕，故非久即敗。

translations.literal: In previous reigns Wang Zhi and Liu Jin, though both were monsters, the paths of remonstrance were clear and officials were kept at a distance from them, so they did not long endure before falling.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier reigns, Wang Zhi and Liu Jin were monsters both, yet the channels of remonstrance remained open and courtiers were kept at a remove from them—so neither lasted long before ruin.

sentences.zh: 今權珰報復，反借言官以伸；

translations.literal: Now the eunuch in power takes revenge, yet uses censorial officials to carry it out;
translations.idiomatic: Today the eunuch in power pursues revenge, yet does so through the censorial corps;

sentences.zh: 言官聲勢，反借權珰以重。

translations.literal: and censorial officials bolster their might by relying on the eunuch in power in return.
translations.idiomatic: and the censorial corps, in turn, inflates its authority by leaning on the eunuch's power.

sentences.zh: 數月以來，熊德陽、江秉謙、侯震旸、王紀、滿朝薦斥矣，鄒元標、馮從吾罷矣，文震孟、鄭鄤逐矣，近且扼孫慎行、盛以弘，而絕其揆路。

translations.literal: For months past, Xiong Deyang, Jiang Bingqian, Hou Zhenyang, Wang Ji, and Man Chao have been denounced and expelled; Zou Yuanbiao and Feng Congwu have been removed from office; Wen Zhenmeng and Zheng Man have been driven out; recently Sun Shenxing and Sheng Yihong have been blocked and denied the path to the grand secretariat.
