translations.idiomatic: For months now, Xiong Deyang, Jiang Bingqian, Hou Zhenyang, Wang Ji, and Man Chao have been impeached and driven out; Zou Yuanbiao and Feng Congwu dismissed; Wen Zhenmeng and Zheng Man banished; and lately Sun Shenxing and Sheng Yihong have been choked off from the route to the grand secretariat.

sentences.zh: 摘瓜抱蔓，正人重足。

translations.literal: Pull one melon and the vine comes with it; upright men tread as though on thin ice.
translations.idiomatic: Pluck one melon and the whole vine follows; honest men walk as if on cracking ice.

sentences.zh: 舉朝各愛一死，無敢明犯其鋒者。

translations.literal: The whole court each cherishes his life and dares not openly confront their sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court clings to life, and none dares meet their edge head-on.

sentences.zh: 臣若尚顧微軀，不為入告，將內有進忠為之指揮，旁有客氏為之羽翼，外有劉朝輩為典兵示威，而又有鞏輩蟻附蠅集，內外交通，驅除善類，天下事尚忍言哉！

translations.literal: If I still cared for my slight person and did not enter my report, there would be Jin Zhong directing from within, Ke Shi supporting from the side, Liu Chao and his ilk controlling troops to show force without, and Gong and company swarming like ants and flies—inside and outside conspiring, expelling the good—and how could one bear to speak of the affairs of the empire!
translations.idiomatic: If I still prized my own skin and held my tongue, Wei Zhongxian would command from within, Ke Shi would shield him from the side, Liu Chao and his kind would parade military power without, and men like Gong would swarm in like ants and flies—inner and outer factions in league, the good driven out—and then who could bear to speak of the fate of the realm!

sentences.zh: 疏入，進忠益怒。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Jin Zhong grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Wei Zhongxian's rage only deepened.

sentences.zh: 率劉朝等環泣帝前，乞自髡以激帝怒。

translations.literal: He led Liu Chao and others to weep in a circle before the emperor, begging to shave their own heads to inflame the emperor's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered Liu Chao and the others to weep in a ring before the emperor, begging to shave their own heads so as to stoke the sovereign's fury.

sentences.zh: 乃令宗建陳交通實狀，將加重譴，宗建回奏益侃直。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Zongjian to state the facts of his collusion, intending to impose heavier punishment; Zongjian's reply grew all the bolder and more forthright.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zongjian to set out the facts of his alleged collusion, intending heavier punishment. Zongjian's reply came back all the bolder.

sentences.zh: 進忠議廷杖之，閣臣力爭，乃止，奪俸。

translations.literal: Jin Zhong proposed beating him at court; grand secretaries argued fiercely against it and it was stopped, though his salary was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian pressed for a beating in open court. The grand secretaries fought the measure to a halt, and Zongjian was spared—though his salary was stripped away.

sentences.zh: 會給事中劉弘化、御史方大任等交章助宗建攻進忠、鞏，鞏復力詆諸人。

translations.literal: At this time Supervising Secretary Liu Honghua, Censor Fang Daren, and others submitted memorials in succession supporting Zongjian's attack on Jin Zhong and Gong; Gong again fiercely slandered them all.
translations.idiomatic: About then, Supervising Secretary Liu Honghua, Censor Fang Daren, and others piled on with memorials backing Zongjian's assault on Wei Zhongxian and Gong. Gong answered with fresh vitriol against them all.

sentences.zh: 詔下諸疏平議，廷臣為兩解之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to review all the memorials impartially, and court officials mediated between both sides.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out ordering all the memorials reviewed on neutral ground, and court officials worked to settle the quarrel between the two camps.

sentences.zh: 乃嚴旨切責，奪鞏、宗建俸三月。

translations.literal: A stern edict then severely rebuked them and docked Gong's and Zongjian's salaries for three months.
translations.idiomatic: A sharp edict followed, rebuking both sides and withholding three months' salary from Gong and Zongjian.

sentences.zh: 是時，劉朝典內操，遂謀行邊。

translations.literal: At this time Liu Chao was in charge of the palace guard and then plotted a tour of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Chao commanded the palace guard and began plotting a personal tour of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 廷臣微聞之，莫敢言。

translations.literal: Court officials faintly heard of it but dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the court in whispers, but no one dared raise the matter openly.

sentences.zh: 宗建曰：「鞏自謂未嘗通內，今誠能出片紙遏朝，吾請為洗交結之名。」

translations.literal: Zongjian said: "Gong claims he has never communicated with the inner court; if he truly can now produce a single note to stop Liu Chao, I will accept clearing his name of collusion.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian said, "Gong insists he has never trafficked with the inner court. If he can now produce a single line to stop Liu Chao, I will gladly clear his name of collusion.

sentences.zh: 鞏噤不敢發。

translations.literal: Gong fell silent and dared not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gong shut his mouth and would not answer.

sentences.zh: 宗建乃抗疏極諫，歷陳三不可、九害。

translations.literal: Zongjian then submitted a defiant memorial strongly remonstrating, setting forth in detail three reasons why it must not be done and nine harms.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian then submitted a defiant memorial of fierce remonstrance, laying out in full three reasons the plan must not proceed and nine harms it would bring.

sentences.zh: 會朝與進忠有隙，事亦中寢。

translations.literal: As it happened Liu Chao and Jin Zhong had a falling-out, and the matter also died in mid-course.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, Liu Chao and Wei Zhongxian had fallen out, and the scheme died halfway to execution.

sentences.zh: 其冬出按湖廣，以憂歸。

translations.literal: That winter he went out on an inspection tour to Huguang and returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he went out on provincial inspection in Huguang, then returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，大學士馮銓銜御史張慎言嘗論己，屬其門生曹欽程誣劾，而以宗建為首，並及李應升、黃尊素。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, Grand Secretary Feng Quan, nursing a grudge because Censor Zhang Shenyan had once criticized him, instructed his disciple Cao Qincheng to lodge a false impeachment, with Zongjian named as ringleader, and also implicating Li Yingsheng and Huang Zunsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year, Grand Secretary Feng Quan, still smarting from Censor Zhang Shenyan's past criticism of him, set his protégé Cao Qincheng to lodge a fabricated impeachment. Zhou Zongjian was named as ringleader, with Li Yingsheng and Huang Zunsu dragged in as well.

sentences.zh: 忠賢遂矯詔削籍，下撫按追贓。

translations.literal: Zhongxian then forged an edict striking them from the rolls and ordered provincial officials to pursue their illicit gains.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian then forged an edict striking them from the official rolls and ordered the provincial governor and surveillance commissioner to recover their ill-gotten wealth.

sentences.zh: 明年以所司具獄緩，遣緹騎逮治。

translations.literal: The next year, because the responsible offices had drawn up a lenient case, he dispatched the imperial guards to arrest and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, finding the responsible offices had prepared too lenient a case, he sent the imperial arresters to seize and punish them.

sentences.zh: 俄入之李實疏中，下詔獄毒訊。

translations.literal: Soon they were included in Li Shi's memorial and sent to the imperial prison for brutal interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they were folded into a memorial by Li Shi and consigned to the imperial prison for savage interrogation.

sentences.zh: 許顯純厲聲罵曰：「復能詈魏上公一丁不識乎！」

translations.literal: Xu Xianchun barked: "Can you still curse the Lord Wei without knowing a single character!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianchun snarled, "Still dare curse Lord Wei when you cannot read a single character!

sentences.zh: 竟坐納廷弼賄萬三千，斃之獄。

translations.literal: In the end he was convicted of accepting thirteen thousand taels in bribes from Tingbi and beaten to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was convicted of taking thirteen thousand taels in bribes from Tingbi and was beaten to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 宗建既死，征贓益急。

translations.literal: After Zongjian died, the pursuit of his illicit gains grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongjian's death, the hunt for his supposed graft grew only fiercer.

sentences.zh: 其所親副使蔣英代之輸，亦坐削籍。

translations.literal: His close associate, Vice Commissioner Jiang Ying, paid on his behalf and was also struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: His close associate, Vice Commissioner Jiang Ying, paid the demanded sum on his behalf and was himself struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，詔贈宗建太仆寺卿，官其一子。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell, an edict posthumously conferred on Zongjian the rank of Grand Master of the Stud and granted office to one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Zhongxian's fall, an edict posthumously honored Zongjian as Grand Master of the Stud and granted office to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚忠毅。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously given the temple name Zhongyi ('Loyal and Steadfast').
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, he was posthumously granted the title Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 蔣英，嘉善人。

translations.literal: Jiang Ying was a native of Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ying was a native of Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，歷知松溪、漳浦、宜興。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination and successively served as magistrate of Songxi, Zhangpu, and Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi degree-holder, he served in turn as magistrate of Songxi, Zhangpu, and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，由南京驗封郎中，出為福建副使，遂遭珰禍。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign, he rose from chief secretary of the Nanjing Verification Bureau to Vice Commissioner of Fujian, and thus suffered calamity from the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianqi Emperor he advanced from chief secretary of the Nanjing Verification Bureau to Fujian Vice Commissioner—and there fell prey to the eunuch faction.

sentences.zh: 忠賢敗，以故官分巡蘇、松，坐事貶秩。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian fell, he returned to his former office to inspect Suzhou and Songjiang, but was demoted in rank on account of some offense.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Zhongxian's downfall, he was restored to his old rank and assigned to inspect Suzhou and Songjiang, but was soon demoted for an offense.

sentences.zh: 未行而宜興民變，上官以英先治宜興，得民心，檄之撫治。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the new post, the people of Yixing rose in revolt; his superiors, knowing that Ying had previously governed Yixing and enjoyed popular support, dispatched him to pacify the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, the people of Yixing rose in revolt. His superiors, recalling that Ying had once governed Yixing and held the people's trust, ordered him to go and restore order.

sentences.zh: 宜興非英所轄，辭不得，則單騎往諭，懲豪家僮客數人，令亂民自獻其首惡，亂遂定。

translations.literal: Yixing was not within his jurisdiction; unable to refuse, he rode alone to reason with them, punished several bully-gentry retainers, ordered the rioters to surrender their ringleaders themselves, and the disorder was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing lay outside his jurisdiction, but he could not refuse. He rode alone to address the crowd, punished several retainers of powerful local houses, demanded that the rioters hand over their own ringleaders, and the unrest subsided.

sentences.zh: 宜興故多豪家，修撰陳於泰、編修陳於鼎兄弟尤橫，遂激民變，群執兵鼓噪，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: Yixing had long had many powerful local clans; the Hanlin Compiler brothers Chen Yutai and Chen Yuding were especially overbearing, which provoked the popular uprising—crowds seized weapons and raised a clamor, their momentum fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing had long been dominated by powerful clans. The Hanlin compiler brothers Chen Yutai and Chen Yuding were especially overbearing, and their conduct sparked the uprising—armed mobs beating drums and roaring until the tumult seemed unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 賴英，事旋定。

translations.literal: Thanks to Ying, the affair was soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Jiang Ying, the crisis was quickly brought under control.

sentences.zh: 而周延儒方枋國，與陳氏有連，銜英，再貶兩秩，遂歸。

translations.literal: But Zhou Yanru was then directing the state and had ties to the Chen family; nursing a grudge against Ying, he had him demoted two ranks again, and Ying then retired home.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhou Yanru was then chief minister and connected to the Chen family. Bearing a grudge against Ying, he had him demoted two more ranks, and Ying retired home.

sentences.zh: 鞏，遷安人。

translations.literal: Gong was a native of Qian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Gong was a native of Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 以附忠賢，驟遷至兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: By attaching himself to Zhongxian, he was rapidly promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: By clinging to Wei Zhongxian's coattails, he was vaulted in short order to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝定逆案，削籍論配。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor settled the cases of treason, Gong was struck from the rolls and sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor adjudicated the treason cases, Gong was struck from the rolls and sentenced to penal exile.

sentences.zh: 我大清拔遷安，鞏遁去，後詣闕自言拒聘，上所撰《卻聘書》。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing took Qian'an; Gong fled. Later he came to the court declaring he had refused employment, and the sovereign composed the 'Declination of Employment.'
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing took Qian'an, and Gong fled. He later came before the throne claiming he had refused service under the new dynasty; the sovereign thereupon composed for him the Declination of Employment.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書梁廷棟論之，下獄坐死。

translations.literal: War Minister Liang Tingdong prosecuted him; he was imprisoned and condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: War Minister Liang Tingdong prosecuted the claim. Gong was thrown into prison and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 巡撫楊嗣昌為訟冤，得遣戍。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Yang Sichang pleaded his case; he was sent into banishment instead.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Yang Sichang pleaded on his behalf, and the sentence was commuted to exile.

sentences.zh: 黃尊素，字真長，余姚人。

translations.literal: Huang Zunsu, courtesy name Zhenchang, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zunsu, styled Zhenchang, was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除寧國推官，精敏強執。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate's assistant of Ningguo, he was sharp, capable, and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed assistant magistrate of Ningguo, he proved keen, efficient, and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，擢御史，謁假歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted to censor and took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted to censor and went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 明年冬還朝，疏請召還余懋衡、曹於汴、劉宗周、周洪謨、王紀、鄒元標、馮從吾，而劾尚書趙秉忠、侍郎牛應元、通政丁啟睿頑鈍。

translations.literal: The next winter he returned to court and memorialized requesting the recall of Yu Maoheng, Cao Yubian, Liu Zongzhou, Zhou Hongmo, Wang Ji, Zou Yuanbiao, and Feng Congwu, while impeaching Ministers Zhao Bingzhong and Niu Yingyuan and Transmission Commissioner Ding Qirui as dull and incompetent.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he returned to court and memorialized for the recall of Yu Maoheng, Cao Yubian, Liu Zongzhou, Zhou Hongmo, Wang Ji, Zou Yuanbiao, and Feng Congwu, while impeaching Ministers Zhao Bingzhong and Niu Yingyuan and Transmission Commissioner Ding Qirui as sluggish and obtuse.

sentences.zh: 秉忠、應元俱引去。

translations.literal: Bingzhong and Yingyuan both withdrew from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingzhong and Niu Yingyuan both resigned.

sentences.zh: 山東妖賊既平，余黨復煽，巡撫王惟儉不能撫馭，尊素疏論之，因言：「巡撫本內外兼用，今盡用京卿，不若揚歷外服者之練習。」

translations.literal: After the demonic bandits of Shandong had been suppressed, remaining partisans stirred again; Grand Coordinator Wang Weijian could not control them. Zunsu memorialized criticizing this, adding: "Grand coordinators were originally drawn from both inside and outside the capital; now using only capital officials exclusively is inferior to those seasoned by service in the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebel cult in Shandong was crushed, surviving followers stirred up trouble again, and Grand Coordinator Wang Weijian could not keep order. Zunsu memorialized against him, adding: "Grand coordinators were once drawn from both capital and provinces alike. To fill the post exclusively with capital officials is far inferior to appointing men tempered by service in the field.

sentences.zh: 又數陳邊事，力詆大將馬世龍，忤樞輔孫承宗意。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly addressed frontier affairs and fiercely denounced General Ma Shilong, offending Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke repeatedly on frontier affairs and savaged General Ma Shilong, crossing Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong in the process.

sentences.zh: 時帝在位數年，未嘗一召見大臣。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had been on the throne several years without once summoning high officials for audience.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had reigned several years without once calling a senior minister to audience.

sentences.zh: 尊素請復便殿召對故事，面決大政，否則講筵之暇，令大臣面商可否。

translations.literal: Zunsu requested restoration of the old practice of audience in the Side Hall to decide great affairs face to face, or otherwise, in the intervals of the lecture sessions, to let ministers discuss matters face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu petitioned for a return to the old custom of holding audience in the Side Hall to decide great affairs in person—or, failing that, to use the intervals of the lecture sessions for ministers to debate policy face to face.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not adopt this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not act on the proposal.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，大風揚沙，晝晦，天鼓鳴，如是者十日。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, great winds raised sand; day turned dim; heaven drums sounded—thus for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, fierce winds whipped sand through the air until daylight dimmed, and heaven drums sounded—ten days of it without cease.

sentences.zh: 三月朔，京師地震三，乾清宮尤甚。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, the capital shook with three earthquakes; the Palace of Heavenly Purity was worst hit.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month, the capital was struck by three earthquakes, the Palace of Heavenly Purity suffering the worst.

sentences.zh: 適帝體違和，人情惶懼。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor's health was impaired and popular sentiment was fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's health was failing at the same time, and fear spread through the populace.

sentences.zh: 尊素力陳時政十失，末言：「陛下厭薄言官，人懷忌諱，遂有剽竊皮毛，莫犯中扃者。

translations.literal: Zunsu vigorously set forth ten failures of current policy, concluding: "Your Majesty disdains and belittles remonstrating officials; men harbor taboos, so there are those who steal scraps of surface doctrine and dare not touch what lies at the heart of power.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu forcefully enumerated ten failures of the age, concluding: "Your Majesty scorns the remonstrating officials. Men walk on eggshells, and so some merely parrot empty phrases, never daring to touch what lies at the heart of power.

sentences.zh: 今阿保重於趙嬈，禁旅近於唐末，蕭墻之憂慘於敵國。

translations.literal: Now favored minions weigh heavier than Zhao Rang and Zhao Yan; the imperial guard resembles the late Tang; anxieties within the palace walls are graver than those of enemy states.
translations.idiomatic: Today favored minions outweigh the Zhao sisters of old; the palace guard recalls the dying days of Tang; and the danger within the palace walls is worse than any threat from abroad.

sentences.zh: 廷無謀幄，邊無折沖，當國者昧安危之機，誤國者護恥敗之局。

translations.literal: The court has no planning tent; the frontier has no breaker of enemy rushes; those holding power are blind to the pivot between safety and peril, and those who harm the state shelter shame in a failing position.
translations.idiomatic: The court has no council of strategy; the frontier has no general to break the enemy's charge. Those who govern cannot read the hinge between safety and ruin, while those who ruin the state cling to a position already steeped in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 不於此進賢退不肖，而疾剛方正直之士如仇仇，陛下獨不為社稷計乎？」

translations.literal: Instead of promoting the worthy and removing the unworthy, you treat upright and principled men as bitter enemies—does Your Majesty alone not consider the altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: Rather than advance the worthy and cast out the unfit, you treat upright and principled men like mortal foes. Does Your Majesty spare no thought at all for the altars of state?

sentences.zh: 疏入，魏忠賢大怒，謀廷杖之。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Wei Zhongxian was greatly angered and plotted to beat him at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Wei Zhongxian flew into a rage and plotted a beating in open court.

sentences.zh: 韓爌力救，乃奪俸一年。

translations.literal: Han Kuang argued fiercely for his rescue, and he was only docked a year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang fought hard to save him, and the punishment was reduced to forfeiture of a year's salary.

sentences.zh: 既而楊漣劾忠賢，被旨譙讓。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yang Lian impeached Zhongxian and received an edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian and was himself rebuked by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 尊素憤，抗疏繼之，略言：「天下有政歸近幸，威福旁移，而世界清明者乎？

translations.literal: Zunsu, indignant, submitted a defiant follow-up memorial stating in part: "Has there ever been a world where government devolves upon favored intimates, authority and favor shift to their side, yet all remains clear and bright?
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu, burning with indignation, submitted a defiant follow-up memorial, writing in part: "Has there ever been an age in which power passed to favored intimates, in which authority and favor shifted into their hands, yet the realm remained clear and bright?

sentences.zh: 天下有中外洶洶，無不欲食其肉，而可置之左右者乎？

translations.literal: Has there ever been one whom court and empire roil against, all wishing to eat his flesh, yet who may still be kept at the sovereign's side?
translations.idiomatic: Has there ever been a man whom court and country alike revile, every soul wishing to tear his flesh from his bones, yet who is still kept at the sovereign's elbow?

sentences.zh: 陛下必以為曲謹可用，不知不小曲謹，不大無忌；

translations.literal: Your Majesty surely thinks that petty cunning makes him usable—not knowing that what is not small in petty cunning is not small in boundless insolence;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty surely believes his petty compliance makes him manageable—not understanding that one who is not small in petty compliance will not be small in boundless audacity;

sentences.zh: 必以為惟吾駕馭，不知不可駕馭，則不可收拾矣。

translations.literal: you surely think only you can rein him in—not knowing that what cannot be reined in cannot afterward be brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: you surely believe only you can rein him in—not understanding that what cannot be reined in cannot afterward be brought under control.

sentences.zh: 陛下登極以來，公卿臺諫累累罷歸，致在位者無固誌。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, grand dukes, ministers, and censorial officials have been dismissed and sent home in streams, so that those who remain have no steadfast resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, ministers and censorial officials have been dismissed and sent home in waves, until those who remain dare hold no firm conviction at all.

sentences.zh: 不於此稱孤立，乃以去一近侍為孤立耶？

translations.literal: Instead of calling this isolation, do you call the removal of one intimate attendant isolation?
translations.idiomatic: If this is not what you call isolation, do you call the dismissal of a single intimate attendant isolation?

sentences.zh: 今忠賢不法狀，廷臣已發露無余，陛下若不早斷，彼形見勢窮，復何顧忌。

translations.literal: Now Zhongxian's unlawful conduct has been fully exposed by court officials without remainder; if Your Majesty does not decide early, when his form appears and his power is exhausted, what scruples will he still have?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's crimes have already been laid bare by court officials down to the last detail. If Your Majesty does not act while there is still time, once he sees his position exposed and his power spent, what will still restrain him?

sentences.zh: 忠賢必不肯收其已縱之韁，而凈滌其腸胃；

translations.literal: Zhongxian will surely be unwilling to gather in the reins he has already slackened and cleanse his bowels and stomach;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian will surely refuse to pull back the reins he has already let slip or to cleanse his corrupt heart;

sentences.zh: 忠賢之私人，必不肯回其已往之棹，而默消其冰山。

translations.literal: Zhongxian's private followers will surely be unwilling to turn back the oars already cast and silently melt away their ice mountains;
translations.idiomatic: His private agents will surely refuse to turn back the course they have already embarked upon or quietly melt away the hidden power they have built;

sentences.zh: 始猶與士大夫為仇，繼將以至尊為註。

translations.literal: At first they were still enemies with scholar-officials; next they will make the sovereign himself the target.
translations.idiomatic: At first they made enemies only of scholar-officials; next they will turn the sovereign himself into their mark.

sentences.zh: 柴柵既固，毒螫誰何？

translations.literal: Once the palisade is firm, who can do anything about the poisonous sting?
translations.idiomatic: Once their barricade is set, who will be able to check their venomous sting?

sentences.zh: 不惟臺諫折之不足，即幹戈取之亦難矣。」

translations.literal: Not only will censorial remonstrance be insufficient to break them; even taking them by force of arms will be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance from the censorate will not suffice to break them—and even armed force will hardly suffice to take them down.

sentences.zh: 忠賢得疏愈恨。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian received the memorial, he hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian received the memorial, his hatred deepened.

sentences.zh: 萬燝既廷杖，又欲杖御史林汝翥，諸言官詣閣爭之。

translations.literal: After Wan Jing had already been beaten at court, he also wished to beat the investigating censor Lin Ruhu; all the remonstrating officials went to the Grand Secretariat to protest.
translations.idiomatic: After Wan Jing had already been beaten in court, the palace also sought to beat investigating censor Lin Ruhu; remonstrating officials went to the Grand Secretariat to protest.

sentences.zh: 小珰數百人擁入閣中，攘臂肆罵，諸閣臣俯首不敢語。

translations.literal: Several hundred petty eunuchs surged into the Grand Secretariat, rolled up their sleeves and cursed freely; the grand secretaries bowed their heads and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred minor eunuchs pushed into the Grand Secretariat, rolled up their sleeves, and cursed at will; the grand secretaries bowed their heads and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 尊素厲聲曰：「內閣絲綸地，即司禮非奉詔不敢至，若輩無禮至此！」

translations.literal: Zunsu said in a stern voice: "The inner cabinet is the place of imperial silk edicts; even the Directorate of Ceremonial does not dare come unless commanded by edict—how dare you people be so rude as to come here!"
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu cried out in a stern voice: "The inner cabinet is where imperial edicts are issued; even the Directorate of Ceremonial does not dare enter without an edict—how dare you be so insolent!

sentences.zh: 乃稍稍散去。

translations.literal: They then gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: At that they gradually dispersed.

sentences.zh: 無何，燝以創重卒。

translations.literal: Before long, Jing died from the severity of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Wan Jing died from the severity of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 尊素上言：「律例，非叛逆十惡無死法。

translations.literal: Zunsu submitted a memorial stating: "By statute and precedent, apart from rebellion and the ten abominations there is no death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu submitted a memorial: "By law, only rebellion and the ten capital offenses carry the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 今以披肝瀝膽之忠臣，竟殞於磨牙礪齒之兇豎。

translations.literal: Now a loyal minister who laid bare his liver and drained his gall has perished at the hands of a vicious wretch grinding and whetting his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Now a loyal minister who poured out his heart and soul has perished at the hands of a vicious scoundrel grinding his teeth for blood.

sentences.zh: 此輩必欣欣相告，吾儕借天子威柄，可鞭笞百僚。

translations.literal: This lot will surely tell one another with delight: "We, borrowing the Son of Heaven's authority, may whip and beat the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: These men will surely rejoice among themselves: "We can wield the Son of Heaven's authority to lash and beat the hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 後世有秉董狐筆，繼朱子《綱目》者，書曰『某月某日，郎中萬燝以言事廷杖死』，豈不上累聖德哉！

translations.literal: In later ages, one who wields Dong Hu's brush and succeeds to Zhu Xi's Outline and Details will write, "On such-and-such month and day, Director Wan Jing died from court beating for speaking on affairs"—would this not tarnish the sacred virtue above?
translations.idiomatic: When some future historian wielding Dong Hu's brush and following Zhu Xi's Outline and Details writes, "On such-and-such date, Director Wan Jing died by court beating for remonstrance," will this not stain Your Majesty's sacred virtue?

sentences.zh: 進廷杖之說者，必曰祖制，不知二正之世，王振、劉瑾為之；

translations.literal: Those who advance the argument for court beating will surely say it is ancestral precedent—not knowing that in the reigns of the two Zheng emperors, Wang Zhen and Liu Jin did it;
translations.idiomatic: Those who advocate court beatings will surely cite ancestral precedent—forgetting that in the reigns of the two Zheng emperors it was Wang Zhen and Liu Jin who introduced them;

sentences.zh: 世祖、神宗之朝，張璁、嚴嵩、張居正為之。

translations.literal: In the reigns of the Founding Ancestor and the Divine Ancestor, Zhang Cong, Yan Song, and Zhang Juzheng did it.
translations.idiomatic: In the reigns of the Hongwu and Wanli emperors, Zhang Cong, Yan Song, and Zhang Juzheng did it.

sentences.zh: 奸人欲有所逞，憚忠臣義士掣其肘，必借廷杖以快其私，使人主蒙拒諫之名，己受乘權之實，而仁賢且有抱蔓之形。

translations.literal: When villainous men wish to have their way, fearing that loyal ministers and righteous scholars will check their elbow, they must borrow court beating to gratify private ends, causing the ruler to bear the name of rejecting remonstrance while they themselves receive the reality of seizing power—and the benevolent and worthy will even take on the appearance of those clinging to the vine.
translations.idiomatic: When villains wish to have their way but fear that loyal ministers will check them, they resort to court beatings to serve their private ends—leaving the ruler with the name of rejecting remonstrance while they seize real power, and leaving the worthy with the appearance of those who cling to a fading vine.

sentences.zh: 於是乎為所欲為，莫有顧忌，而禍即移之國家。

translations.literal: Thereupon they do as they please without any scruples, and calamity shifts onto the state.
translations.idiomatic: Then they do as they please without restraint, and the calamity falls upon the state.

sentences.zh: 燝今已矣，辱士殺士，漸不可開。

translations.literal: Jing is gone now; humiliating scholars and killing scholars—this evil cannot be allowed to spread.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Jing is gone now; to humiliate scholars and kill them is a breach that must not be opened.

sentences.zh: 乞復故官，破格賜恤，俾遺孤得扶櫬還鄉，燝死且不朽。」

translations.literal: I beg that his former office be restored, that extraordinary mourning gifts be granted, so that his orphaned survivors may bear his coffin home—and Jing's death will not have been in vain."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that his former rank be restored and extraordinary posthumous honors granted, so his orphaned family may carry his coffin home—and Wan Jing's death will not have been in vain.

sentences.zh: 疏入，益忤忠賢意。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it further offended Zhongxian's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, it further provoked Wei Zhongxian's wrath.

sentences.zh: 八月，河南進玉璽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Henan presented a jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Henan presented a jade seal.

sentences.zh: 忠賢欲侈其事，命由大明門進，行受璽禮，百僚表賀。

translations.literal: Zhongxian wished to magnify the event, ordering entry through the Great Ming Gate, the performance of the seal-receiving rite, and congratulatory memorials from the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian wished to lavish ceremony upon the affair, ordering that the seal enter through the Great Ming Gate, that the seal-receiving rite be performed, and that the hundred officials submit congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 尊素上言：「昔宋哲宗得璽，蔡確等競言祥瑞，改年元符，宋祚卒不競。

translations.literal: Zunsu submitted a memorial stating: "Formerly, when Emperor Zhezong of Song obtained a seal, Cai Que and others competed to call it an auspicious portent and changed the reign title to Yuanfu; yet the Song dynasty did not endure.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu submitted a memorial: "When Emperor Zhezong of Song obtained a seal, Cai Que and others vied to call it an auspicious omen and changed the reign title to Yuanfu—yet the Song dynasty still did not endure.

sentences.zh: 本朝弘治時，陜西獻玉璽，止令取進，給賞五金。

translations.literal: In our dynasty during the Hongzhi reign, when Shaanxi presented a jade seal, the order was merely to have it brought in and a reward of the five metals given.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty during the Hongzhi reign, when Shaanxi presented a jade seal, the court merely had it brought in and gave a reward of the five metals.

sentences.zh: 此祖宗故事，宜從。」

translations.literal: This is the precedent of our ancestors; it should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: This is the precedent of our forebears and should be followed.

sentences.zh: 事獲中止。

translations.literal: The affair was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was halted.

sentences.zh: 五年春，遣視陜西茶馬。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, he was sent to inspect the tea-and-horse trade in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, he was dispatched to inspect the tea-and-horse trade in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 甫出都，逆黨曹欽程劾其專擊善類，助高攀龍、魏大中虐焰，遂削籍。

translations.literal: Just after leaving the capital, the factional opponent Cao Qincheng impeached him for exclusively attacking worthy men and fueling the cruel flames of Gao Panlong and Wei Dazhong; he was then stripped from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he left the capital when the factional enemy Cao Qincheng impeached him for singling out worthy men for attack and fanning the persecutions of Gao Panlong and Wei Dazhong; he was then struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 尊素謇諤敢言，尤有深識遠慮。

translations.literal: Zunsu was upright and outspoken, and possessed especially deep insight and far-reaching foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu was upright and outspoken, with especially deep insight and far-reaching foresight.

sentences.zh: 初入臺，鄒元標實援之，即進規曰：「都門非講學地，徐文貞已叢議於前矣。」

translations.literal: When he first entered the censorate, Zou Yuanbiao had in fact recommended him; he immediately offered counsel, saying: "The capital is not a place for lecturing on learning; Xu Wenzhen already met with clustered criticism before this."
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the censorate, Zou Yuanbiao had recommended him; he immediately offered counsel: "The capital is not a place for public lecturing; Xu Wenzhen had already drawn fierce criticism for it.

sentences.zh: 元標不能用。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbiao did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 楊漣將擊忠賢，魏大中以告，尊素曰：「除君側者，必有內援。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian was about to strike at Zhongxian, Wei Dazhong told him; Zunsu said: "To remove one at the ruler's side, one must have inner support.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian was about to move against Wei Zhongxian, Wei Dazhong told Zunsu; Zunsu said: "To remove a favorite at the ruler's side, one must have backing within the palace.

sentences.zh: 楊公有之乎？

translations.literal: Does Lord Yang have it?
translations.idiomatic: Does Lord Yang have that?

sentences.zh: 一不中，吾儕無噍類矣。」

translations.literal: If it fails once, none of us will be left alive."
translations.idiomatic: If it fails once, none of us will survive.

sentences.zh: 萬燝死，尊素諷漣去，漣不從，卒及於禍。

translations.literal: After Wan Jing died, Zunsu admonished Lian to withdraw; Lian did not follow, and in the end met with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After Wan Jing died, Zunsu urged Lian to withdraw; Lian refused, and in the end met with disaster.

sentences.zh: 大中將劾魏廣微，尊素曰：「廣微，小人之包羞者也，攻之急，則鋌而走險矣。」

translations.literal: When Dazhong was about to impeach Wei Guangwei, Zunsu said: "Guangwei is the sort of petty man who knows shame; press the attack hard and he will run to extremes."
translations.idiomatic: When Dazhong was about to impeach Wei Guangwei, Zunsu said: "Guangwei is a petty man who still knows shame; press him too hard and he will take desperate measures.

sentences.zh: 大中不從，廣微益合於忠賢，以興大難。

translations.literal: Dazhong did not follow; Guangwei all the more aligned with Zhongxian, giving rise to the great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong did not heed him; Guangwei drew all the closer to Wei Zhongxian, and the great calamity ensued.

sentences.zh: 是時，東林盈朝，自以鄉里分朋黨。

translations.literal: At that time the Donglin faction filled the court, dividing themselves into cliques by native place.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Donglin faction dominated the court, dividing themselves into cliques by native place.

sentences.zh: 江西章允儒、陳良訓與大中有隙，而大中欲駁尚書南師仲恤典，秦人亦多不悅。

translations.literal: Jiangxi's Zhang Yunru and Chen Liangxun had a rift with Dazhong, and Dazhong wished to reject the mourning gifts for Minister Nan Shizhong; many from Qin also were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunru and Chen Liangxun of Jiangxi were at odds with Dazhong; Dazhong also wished to reject the mourning honors for Minister Nan Shizhong, which displeased many from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尊素急言於大中，止之。

translations.literal: Zunsu urgently spoke to Dazhong and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu urgently spoke to Dazhong and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 最後，山西尹同臯、潘雲翼欲用其座主郭尚友為山西巡撫，大中以尚友數問遺朝貴，執不可。

translations.literal: Finally, Shanxi's Yin Tonggao and Pan Yunyi wished to appoint their patron Guo Shangyou as Shanxi grand coordinator; Dazhong, because Shangyou had repeatedly sent gifts to court magnates, insisted it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Finally, Yin Tonggao and Pan Yunyi of Shanxi wished to appoint their patron Guo Shangyou as grand coordinator of Shanxi; Dazhong, citing Shangyou's repeated gifts to court magnates, adamantly refused.

sentences.zh: 尊素引杜征南數遺洛中貴要為言，大中卒不可，議用謝應祥，難端遂作。

translations.literal: Zunsu cited Du Zhengnan's repeated gifts to eunuch powers in Luoyang as a parallel, yet Dazhong ultimately would not yield; they settled on Xie Yingxiang, and the source of trouble arose.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsu cited how Du Zhengnan had repeatedly sent gifts to eunuch powers in Luoyang, but Dazhong still would not yield; the nomination fell to Xie Yingxiang, and trouble began from there.

sentences.zh: 汪文言初下獄，忠賢即欲羅織諸人。

translations.literal: When Wang Wényan was first thrown into prison, Zhongxian immediately wished to entrap the various men in a fabricated case.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wényan was first imprisoned, Wei Zhongxian immediately sought to frame the others in a fabricated case.

sentences.zh: 已，知為尊素所解，恨甚。

translations.literal: Afterward, learning that Zunsu had unraveled it, he hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Learning afterward that Zunsu had thwarted the scheme, Wei Zhongxian hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 其黨亦以尊素多智慮，欲殺之。

translations.literal: His faction also, because Zunsu was full of shrewd planning, wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: His faction also wished him dead, knowing how shrewd Zunsu was.

sentences.zh: 會吳中訛言尊素欲效楊一清誅劉瑾，用李實為張永，授以秘計。

translations.literal: It happened that a rumor in Wu said Zunsu wished to follow Yang Yiqing's execution of Liu Jin, using Li Shi as Zhang Yong and entrusting him with a secret plan.
translations.idiomatic: A rumor spread in Wu that Zunsu meant to imitate Yang Yiqing's execution of Liu Jin—using Li Shi in the role Zhang Yong had played—and had entrusted him with a secret plan.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大懼，遣刺事者至吳中凡四輩。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly afraid and sent four parties of secret agents to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was greatly alarmed and sent four groups of secret agents to Wu.

sentences.zh: 侍郎烏程沈演家居，奏記忠賢曰：「事有跡矣。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister Shen Yan of Wucheng, living at home, wrote to Zhongxian saying: "There are already traces of the affair."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Shen Yan of Wucheng, living in retirement, wrote to Wei Zhongxian: "There are already signs of the plot.

sentences.zh: 於是日遣使譙訶實，取其空印白疏，入尊素等七人姓名，遂被逮。

translations.literal: Thereupon they daily sent envoys to rebuke and denounce Li Shi, took his blank-seal memorial, inserted the names of Zunsu and six others, and he was then arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they sent envoys day after day to berate Li Shi, seized a blank-seal memorial from him, inserted the names of Zunsu and six others, and the arrests followed.

sentences.zh: 使者至蘇州，適城中擊殺逮周順昌旗尉，其城外人並擊逮尊素者。

translations.literal: When the envoys reached Suzhou, it happened that within the city people killed the banner guards sent to arrest Zhou Shunchang; outside the city people also attacked those sent to arrest Zunsu.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys reached Suzhou, the populace within the city had killed the banner guards sent to arrest Zhou Shunchang; outside the city they also attacked those sent to arrest Zunsu.

sentences.zh: 逮者失駕帖，不敢至。

translations.literal: The arresting officers lost their warrant tablets and dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The arresting officers lost their warrant tablets and dared not enter the city.

sentences.zh: 尊素聞，即囚服詣吏，自投詔獄。

translations.literal: When Zunsu heard, he immediately put on prisoner garb and went to the officials, surrendering himself to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunsu heard of this, he put on prisoner garb and presented himself to the officials, surrendering to the imperial prison of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 許顯純、崔應元搒掠備至，勒贓二千八百，五日一追比。

translations.literal: Xu Xianchun and Cui Yingyuan tortured him to the fullest, forcing confession of embezzlement of 2,800 taels, with collection demanded every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianchun and Cui Yingyuan tortured him relentlessly, forcing a confession of embezzlement totaling 2,800 taels and demanding payment every five days.

sentences.zh: 已，知獄卒將害己，叩首謝君父，賦詩一章，遂死，時六年閏六月朔日也，年四十三。

translations.literal: Afterward, knowing the prison guards intended to kill him, he kowtowed in thanks to his ruler and father, composed one poem, and died—on the first day of the intercalary sixth month of the sixth year; he was forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the prison guards meant to kill him, he kowtowed in farewell to his sovereign and composed a final poem before he died—on the first day of the intercalary sixth month of the sixth year; he was forty-three.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太仆卿，任一子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, and one son was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and one son was granted office.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚忠端。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, he was posthumously given the temple name Zhongduan (Loyal and Upright).
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, he was posthumously given the posthumous title Zhongduan—Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 李應升，字仲達，江陰人。

translations.literal: Li Yingsheng, styled Zhongda, was a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yingsheng, styled Zhongda, was a native of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授南康推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 出無辜十九人於死，置大猾數人重辟。

translations.literal: He released nineteen innocent men from death and imposed severe punishments on several great ruffians.
translations.idiomatic: He saved nineteen innocent men from death and imposed heavy punishments on several notorious criminals.

sentences.zh: 士民服其公廉，為之謠曰：「前林後李，清和無比。」

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners admired his fairness and integrity and made a rhyme for him saying: "Before Lin, after Li—pure and mild beyond compare."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners admired his fairness and integrity and made a rhyme about him: "Before Lin, after Li—pure and mild beyond compare."

sentences.zh: 林謂晉江林學曾，卒官南京戶部侍郎，以清慎著稱者也。

translations.literal: Lin refers to Lin Xuezeng of Jinjiang, who ended his career as Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue and was renowned for purity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Lin" refers to Lin Xuezeng of Jinjiang, who ended his career as Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue and was renowned for purity and prudence.

sentences.zh: 九江、南康間有柯、陳二大族，相傳陳友諒苗裔，負固強梗，嘗拒捕，有司議兵之。

translations.literal: Between Jiujiang and Nankang there were two great clans, the Ke and the Chen, said to be descendants of Chen Youliang; stubborn and violent, they once resisted arrest, and the local officials debated sending troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jiujiang and Nankang were two powerful clans, the Ke and the Chen, said to be descendants of Chen Youliang; entrenched and violent, they once resisted arrest, and officials debated sending troops against them.

sentences.zh: 應升單騎往諭，皆叩頭聽命，出所匿罪人，一方以定。

translations.literal: Yingsheng went alone on horseback to instruct them; all kowtowed and obeyed, surrendering the criminals they had hidden, and the region was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsheng rode alone to address them; all kowtowed in submission, surrendering the criminals they had sheltered, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，征授御史，謁假歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was summoned and appointed investigating censor; he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was summoned and appointed investigating censor; he took leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，還朝。

translations.literal: The next autumn he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 時天子暗弱，庶政怠弛。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was dim and weak, and common administration was lax and slack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was weak and ineffective, and government had grown slack throughout.

sentences.zh: 應升上疏曰：「方今遼土淪沒，黔、蜀用兵，紅夷之焰未息，西部之賞日增；

translations.literal: Yingsheng submitted a memorial saying: "At present Liaodong territory has fallen; troops are deployed in Qian and Shu; the flames of the Red Barbarians have not ceased; rewards for the western frontier increase daily;
translations.idiomatic: Yingsheng submitted a memorial: "Liaodong has fallen; armies fight in Guizhou and Sichuan; the Dutch threat has not abated; payments to the western frontier grow daily;

sentences.zh: 逃兵肆掠於畿輔，窮民待盡於催科。

translations.literal: Deserters plunder freely in the capital region; the destitute await exhaustion under tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters plunder freely around the capital; the destitute are driven to destitution by tax levies.

sentences.zh: 逗遛習慣，大將畏敵而不敢前；

translations.literal: Delay has become habitual; great generals fear the enemy and dare not advance;
translations.idiomatic: Delay has become habit; great generals fear the enemy and dare not advance;

sentences.zh: 法紀陵夷，驕兵鼓噪而弗能問。

translations.literal: Law and discipline decline; arrogant soldiers beat drums and clamor yet none can be called to account.
translations.idiomatic: Law and discipline decay; arrogant soldiers clamor in mutiny, yet no one can hold them to account.

sentences.zh: 在在增官，日日會議；

translations.literal: Everywhere offices increase, every day conferences are held;
translations.idiomatic: Offices multiply everywhere, meetings are held every day;

sentences.zh: 覆疏衍為故套，嚴旨等若空言。

translations.literal: Reply memorials spin out the same old formulas; stern edicts count as empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Reply memorials rehash the same formulas; stern edicts ring as empty words.

sentences.zh: 陛下不先振竦精神，發皇誌氣，群臣孰肯任怨以破情面之世界者？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not first shake awake your spirit and stir your imperial resolve, which minister will be willing to bear resentment to break this world of personal favor?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not first rouse your spirit and summon your imperial resolve, which minister will dare bear resentment to break this world built on personal connections?

sentences.zh: 祖宗有早午晚三朝，猶時禦便殿咨訪時政。

translations.literal: The ancestors held three audiences—morning, noon, and evening—and still from time to time held counsel in the side hall on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Our forebears held audiences morning, noon, and evening, and still from time to time consulted on affairs of state from the side hall.

sentences.zh: 願俯納臣言，奮然力行，天下事尚可為也。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to bow and accept my words, rise up and act forcefully—affairs under Heaven can still be set right."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed my words, act with resolve, and then affairs under Heaven may still be saved.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復陳時政，略曰：「今天下敝壞極矣，在君臣奮興而力圖之。

translations.literal: Before long, he again presented current policy, stating in part: "Today the realm is broken to the utmost; it depends on ruler and ministers rousing themselves and striving with force.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he again addressed current affairs, writing in part: "The realm is broken to the utmost; salvation depends on ruler and ministers rousing themselves to act with force.

sentences.zh: 陛下振紀綱，則片紙若霆；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty restores discipline and statutes, then a slip of paper is like thunder;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty restores discipline and order, a single edict will land like thunder;

sentences.zh: 大臣捐私曲，則千里運掌；

translations.literal: If great ministers discard private crookedness, then a thousand li is operated in the palm;
translations.idiomatic: If great ministers set aside private interest, governance at a thousand li's remove will move at their fingertips;

sentences.zh: 臺諫任糾彈，則百司飲冰。

translations.literal: If censors and remonstrators take up impeachment, then the hundred offices drink ice.
translations.idiomatic: If censors and remonstrators take up impeachment, the hundred offices will tremble like men swallowing ice;

sentences.zh: 今動議增官，為人營窟，紛紜遷徙，名實乖張。

translations.literal: Now at every turn offices are increased, dens are built for others, appointments shift in confusion, and names and realities diverge.
translations.idiomatic: Now at every turn new offices are proposed, dens are carved out for favorites, appointments shuffle without end, and titles and realities no longer match.

sentences.zh: 自登、萊增巡撫，而侵冒百余萬；

translations.literal: Since adding a grand coordinator for Deng and Lai, more than a million has been embezzled;
translations.idiomatic: Since a grand coordinator was added for Dengzhou and Laizhou, more than a million taels have been embezzled;

sentences.zh: 增招練監軍，而侵冒又十余萬。

translations.literal: After adding supervisors for recruitment and training troops, another hundred thousand plus was embezzled.
translations.idiomatic: After adding supervisors for recruitment and training, another hundred thousand plus was embezzled.

sentences.zh: 邊關內地，將領如蟻，剝軍侵饟，又不知幾十萬。

translations.literal: At frontier passes and in the interior, generals swarm like ants; stripping the army and stealing rations—again one cannot know how many hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontiers and in the interior, generals swarm like ants; stripping troops and stealing rations—who knows how many hundreds of thousands more.

sentences.zh: 增置總督，何補塞垣；

translations.literal: Adding governors-general—what does it supplement at the frontier walls?
translations.idiomatic: What do added governors-general contribute to the frontier defenses?

sentences.zh: 增置京堂，何裨政事。

translations.literal: Adding capital-rank officials—what do they benefit in government affairs?
translations.idiomatic: What do added capital-rank officials contribute to governance?

sentences.zh: 樞貳添註矣，孰慷慨以行邊；

translations.literal: Deputy posts at the military commission have been added by notation—who goes forth to the frontier with generous resolve?
translations.idiomatic: Deputy posts at the military commission have been stacked on—yet who boldly goes to serve on the frontier?

sentences.zh: 司空添註矣，孰拮據以儲備；

translations.literal: Vice minister posts at the Works have been added by notation—who pinches and saves for stores?
translations.idiomatic: Vice minister posts at the Ministry of Works have been stacked on—yet who scrimps to build reserves?

sentences.zh: 大將添註矣，只工媒孽而縱逋逃；

translations.literal: Great general posts have been added by notation—yet they only craft slanders and let deserters go free;
translations.idiomatic: Great general posts have been stacked on—yet the holders only craft slanders and let deserters slip away;

sentences.zh: 禮、兵司屬添註二三十人矣，誰儲邊才而精典禮。

translations.literal: Twenty or thirty subordinates in the Ritual and War ministries have been added by notation—who stores up frontier talent or masters ritual and ceremony?
translations.idiomatic: Twenty or thirty junior posts in the Ministries of Rites and War have been stacked on—yet who grooms frontier talent or masters ritual and ceremony?

sentences.zh: 濫開邊俸，捷徑燃灰，則吏治日壞；

translations.literal: Indiscriminately opening frontier salaries, shortcuts fanning to ash—then official governance worsens daily;
translations.idiomatic: Indiscriminate frontier salaries and shortcuts that burn like kindling will only worsen governance day by day;

sentences.zh: 白衣攘臂，邪人入幕，則奸弁充斥。

translations.literal: Men in white garb roll up their sleeves, wicked men enter staff positions—then treacherous officers fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners thrust themselves forward, unworthy men enter staff posts—and treacherous officers fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 臣請斷自聖心，一切報罷。」

translations.literal: Your subject asks that Your Majesty decide from your sacred heart and reject all of them outright."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide from your own sacred judgment and reject all of these appointments outright.

sentences.zh: 又言：「今事下部曹，十九寢閣，宜重申國典，明正將領之罪。

translations.literal: He also said: "Now when affairs go to the ministries, nine times in ten they are shelved; the national precedents should be reaffirmed and the crimes of generals openly punished.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Now when matters reach the ministries, nine in ten are shelved; the national precedents should be reaffirmed and the crimes of generals openly punished.

sentences.zh: 錦衣旗尉，半歸權要，宜遣官巡視，如京營之制。

translations.literal: The banner guards of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, half fall to powerful figures; officials should be dispatched to inspect them, as with the capital garrison system.
translations.idiomatic: Half the banner guards of the Embroidered Uniform Guard serve powerful patrons; inspectors should be dispatched as with the capital garrison system.

sentences.zh: 衛官襲職，比試不嚴，宜申明舊章，無使幸進將校蠶食。

translations.literal: For guard officers inheriting posts, comparative examinations are not strict; the old regulations should be reaffirmed so that officers who advance by luck do not devour the ranks like silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: For guard officers inheriting their posts, comparative examinations are lax; the old regulations should be reaffirmed so that lucky officers do not devour the ranks like silkworms.

sentences.zh: 逃軍不招，私募乞兒，半分其饟，宜力為創懲。

translations.literal: Deserters are not recruited back; private soldiers hire beggar boys and split half the rations with them—this should be sternly punished as a new offense.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters go unrecalled while officers privately hire beggar boys and split rations with them—this should be sternly punished.

sentences.zh: 窮民敲撲，號哭滿庭，奸吏侵漁，福堂安坐，宜嚴其法制。」

translations.literal: The destitute are beaten and flogged, wailing filling the court; corrupt officials plunder while sitting at ease in their halls of fortune—the law should be strictly enforced."
translations.idiomatic: The destitute are beaten until the court rings with wailing; corrupt officials plunder at will while sitting at ease in their halls—the law should be strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time his advice could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his advice went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 俄劾南京都御史王永光庇部郎範得誌，顛倒公論，永光尋自引去。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Nanjing censor-in-chief Wang Yongguang for shielding department director Fan Dezhi and inverting public opinion; Yongguang soon resigned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he impeached Nanjing censor-in-chief Wang Yongguang for shielding department director Fan Dezhi and reversing public opinion; Yongguang soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，疏陳外番、內盜及小人三患，譏切近習，魏忠賢惡之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, he submitted a memorial setting forth three calamities—foreign tribes, internal bandits, and petty men—and satirizing favored intimates; Wei Zhongxian hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, he submitted a memorial on three calamities—foreign tribes, internal bandits, and petty men—and satirized favored intimates; Wei Zhongxian hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 已，復疏陳民隱，言有十害宜急除，五反宜急去，帝為戒飭所司。

translations.literal: Afterward, he again submitted a memorial on the people's hidden sufferings, stating ten harms that should be urgently removed and five reversals that should be urgently cast off; the emperor issued admonitions to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he again submitted a memorial on the people's hidden sufferings, listing ten harms to remove urgently and five reversals to abandon urgently; the emperor issued admonitions to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 京師一日地三震，疏請保護聖躬，速停內操。

translations.literal: The capital experienced three earthquakes in one day; he submitted a memorial asking that the sacred person be protected and inner drill be halted at once.
translations.idiomatic: The capital experienced three earthquakes in one day; he submitted a memorial asking that the emperor's person be protected and inner drill halted at once.

sentences.zh: 忠賢領東廠，好用立枷，有重三百斤者，不數日即死，先後死者六七十人。

translations.literal: Zhongxian headed the Eastern Depot and liked to use standing cangues; some weighed three hundred jin, and within a few days the victim would die—sixty or seventy died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian headed the Eastern Depot and favored standing cangues; some weighed three hundred jin, and victims died within days—sixty or seventy in succession.

sentences.zh: 應升極言宜罷，忠賢大恨。

translations.literal: Yingsheng spoke forcefully that this should be abolished; Zhongxian hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsheng spoke forcefully that this practice should be abolished; Wei Zhongxian hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 應升知忠賢必禍國，密草疏列其十六罪，將上，為兄所知，攘其疏毀之，怏怏而止。

translations.literal: Yingsheng knew Zhongxian would surely bring calamity on the state; he secretly drafted a memorial listing sixteen of his crimes and was about to submit it when his elder brother learned of it, seized the memorial and destroyed it, and he stopped in vexation.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsheng knew Wei Zhongxian would ruin the state; he secretly drafted a memorial listing sixteen crimes and was about to submit it when his elder brother learned of it, seized and destroyed the memorial, and he stopped in frustration.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾忠賢，得嚴旨，應升憤，即抗疏繼之。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian impeached Zhongxian and received a stern edict, Yingsheng, indignant, immediately submitted a defiant follow-up memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian and received a stern edict, Yingsheng, indignant, immediately submitted a defiant follow-up memorial.

sentences.zh: 中言：「從來奄人之禍，其始莫不有小忠小信以固結主心，根株既深，毒手乃肆。

translations.literal: In the middle he wrote: "From of old the calamity of eunuchs has never failed to begin with small loyalty and small trust to bind the ruler's heart; once the roots run deep, the poisonous hand is unleashed.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle he wrote: "From of old the calamity of eunuchs always begins with small loyalties and small trusts to bind the ruler's heart; once the roots run deep, the poisonous hand is unleashed.

sentences.zh: 今陛下明知其罪，曲賜包容。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty clearly knows his crimes yet indulgently grants him shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty clearly knows his crimes yet indulgently shelters him.

sentences.zh: 彼緩則圖自全之計，急則作走險之謀。

translations.literal: When unhurried he plots plans for self-preservation; when pressed he makes desperate schemes.
translations.idiomatic: When unhurried he plots for self-preservation; when pressed he turns to desperate measures.

sentences.zh: 蕭墻之間，能無隱禍？

translations.literal: Within the palace walls, can hidden calamity be avoided?
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace walls, can hidden calamity be avoided?

sentences.zh: 故忠賢一日不去，則陛下一日不安。

translations.literal: Therefore as long as Zhongxian is not removed, Your Majesty cannot be at ease for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore as long as Wei Zhongxian is not removed, Your Majesty cannot be at ease for a single day.

sentences.zh: 臣為陛下計，莫如聽忠賢引退，以全其命；

translations.literal: Your subject, planning for Your Majesty, advises nothing so well as allowing Zhongxian to withdraw and thereby preserve his life;
translations.idiomatic: I advise Your Majesty to allow Wei Zhongxian to withdraw and thereby preserve his life;

sentences.zh: 為忠賢計，亦莫若早自引決，以乞帷蓋之恩。

translations.literal: planning for Zhongxian as well, nothing so well as early self-withdrawal to beg the grace of the canopy and cover.
translations.idiomatic: and for Wei Zhongxian himself, nothing so well as early withdrawal to beg the grace of imperial protection.

sentences.zh: 不然惡稔貫盈，他日欲保首領，不可得矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, when evil is fully ripe and overflowing, another day you will wish to keep your head and will not be able to."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, when evil is fully ripe, another day you will wish to keep your head and will not be able to.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「君側不清，安用彼相。

translations.literal: He also said: "If those at the ruler's side are not cleared, of what use is that chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "If those at the ruler's side are not cleared, of what use is that chancellor?

sentences.zh: 一時寵利有盡，千秋青史難欺。

translations.literal: Favor and profit for a time have their limit; the green history of a thousand autumns cannot be deceived.
translations.idiomatic: Favor and profit for a time have their limit; the annals of a thousand autumns cannot be deceived.

sentences.zh: 不欲為劉健、謝遷者，並不能為東陽。

translations.literal: Those who do not wish to be Liu Jian and Xie Qian cannot be Dong Yang either.
translations.idiomatic: Those who do not wish to be Liu Jian and Xie Qian cannot be Li Dongyang either.

sentences.zh: 倘畫策投歡，不幾與焦芳同傳耶？」

translations.literal: If you instead plot to win favor, will you not share a biography with Jiao Fang?"
translations.idiomatic: If you instead plot to win favor, will you not share a biography with Jiao Fang?"

sentences.zh: 時魏廣微方深結忠賢，為之謀主，知應升譏己，大恨。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Guangwei was deeply aligned with Zhongxian as his strategist; knowing Yingsheng satirized him, he hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Guangwei was deeply aligned with Wei Zhongxian as his strategist; knowing Yingsheng satirized him, he hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 萬燝之死也，應升極言廷杖不可再，士氣不可折，譏切忠賢輩甚至。

translations.literal: When Wan Jing died, Yingsheng spoke forcefully that court beating must not be repeated and scholar-official morale must not be broken, satirizing Zhongxian's faction to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan Jing died, Yingsheng spoke forcefully that court beatings must not be repeated and scholar-official morale must not be broken, satirizing Wei Zhongxian's faction to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 已，代高攀龍草疏劾崔呈秀。

translations.literal: Afterward, he drafted on Gao Panlong's behalf a memorial impeaching Cui Chengxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he drafted on Gao Panlong's behalf a memorial impeaching Cui Chengxiu.

sentences.zh: 呈秀窘，昏夜款門，長跪乞哀，應升正色固拒，含怒而去。

translations.literal: Chengxiu, cornered, came knocking at his door in the dead of night, knelt long and begged for mercy; Yingsheng sternly refused, and Chengxiu left in rage.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu, cornered, came knocking at his door in the dead of night and knelt long begging for mercy; Yingsheng sternly refused, and Chengxiu left in rage.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，帝廟享頒歷，廣微後至，為魏大中等所糾。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, when the emperor distributed calendars at the ancestral temple audience, Guangwei arrived late and was impeached by Wei Dazhong and others.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month, when the emperor distributed calendars at the ancestral temple audience, Guangwei arrived late and was impeached by Wei Dazhong and others.

sentences.zh: 廣微恚，辨疏詆言者。

translations.literal: Guangwei, enraged, submitted a defense memorial slandering the accusers.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei, enraged, submitted a defense memorial slandering the accusers.

sentences.zh: 應升復抗疏論之，且曰：「廣微父允貞為言官，得罪輔臣以去，聲施至今。

translations.literal: Yingsheng again submitted a defiant memorial discussing it, and said: "Guangwei's father Yunzhen was a remonstrating official who left office after offending a chief minister—his reputation endures to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsheng again submitted a defiant memorial on the matter, writing: "Guangwei's father Yunzhen was a remonstrating official who left office after offending a chief minister—his reputation endures to this day.

sentences.zh: 廣微奈何比言官路馬，斥為此輩？

translations.literal: How can Guangwei compare remonstrating officials to roadside horses and dismiss them as this lot?
translations.idiomatic: How can Guangwei compare remonstrating officials to roadside horses and dismiss them as this lot?

sentences.zh: 夫不與此輩為伍者，必別與一輩為緣。

translations.literal: One who will not stand with this lot must stand with some other lot instead.
translations.idiomatic: One who will not stand with this lot must stand with some other lot instead.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下戒諭廣微，退讀父書，保其家聲，毋倚三窟，與言官為難，他日庶可見乃父地下。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to admonish Guangwei, withdraw and read his father's writings, preserve his family's reputation, not rely on three burrows, and not make enemies of remonstrating officials—then someday he may yet meet his father in the underworld."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to admonish Guangwei to withdraw and read his father's writings, preserve his family's reputation, not rely on three burrows, and not make enemies of remonstrating officials—then someday he may yet meet his father in the underworld.

sentences.zh: 廣微益怒，謀之忠賢，將鐫秩。

translations.literal: Guangwei grew angrier still, plotted with Zhongxian, and sought to demote Yingsheng's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei grew angrier still, plotted with Wei Zhongxian, and sought to demote Yingsheng's rank.

sentences.zh: 首輔韓爌力救，乃奪祿一年。

translations.literal: Chief minister Han Kuang argued fiercely for his rescue, and he was only docked a year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Han Kuang fought hard to save him, and the punishment was reduced to forfeiture of a year's salary.

sentences.zh: 其月，趙南星等悉被逐，朝事大變。

translations.literal: That month, Zhao Nanxing and the rest were all driven out, and court affairs changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Zhao Nanxing and the rest were all driven out, and court affairs changed greatly.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，工部主事曹欽程劾應升護法東林，遂削籍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, Works Ministry director Cao Qincheng impeached Yingsheng for shielding the Donglin faction's laws, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year, Works Ministry director Cao Qincheng impeached Yingsheng for shielding the Donglin faction's laws, and he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 忠賢恨未已。

translations.literal: Zhongxian's hatred was still not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's hatred was still not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，假李實劾周起元疏，入應升名。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, using Li Shi's impeachment memorial against Zhou Qiyuan, they inserted Yingsheng's name.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year, using Li Shi's impeachment memorial against Zhou Qiyuan, they inserted Yingsheng's name.

sentences.zh: 遂逮下詔獄，酷掠，坐贓三千。

translations.literal: He was then arrested and thrown into the imperial prison, tortured cruelly, and convicted of embezzling three thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: He was then arrested and thrown into the imperial prison, tortured cruelly, and convicted of embezzling three thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 尋於閏六月二日斃之，年甫三十四。

translations.literal: Soon, on the second day of the intercalary sixth month, he was killed; he was only thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on the second day of the intercalary sixth month, he was killed; he was only thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太仆卿，錄一子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, and one son was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and one son was granted office.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚忠毅。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, he was posthumously given the posthumous title Zhongyi—Loyal and Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, he was posthumously given the posthumous title Zhongyi—Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 萬燝，字暗夫，南昌人，兵部侍郎恭孫也。

translations.literal: Wan Jing, styled Anfu, was a native of Nanchang and grandson of Vice Minister of War Wan Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Jing, styled Anfu, was a native of Nanchang and grandson of Vice Minister of War Wan Gong.

sentences.zh: 少好學，砥礪名行。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and honed his reputation and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and honed his reputation and conduct.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷四十四年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of Wanli and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of Wanli and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏論刑獄幹和。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial discussing interference in criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial discussing interference in criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 天啟初元，兵事棘，工部需才，調燝工部營繕主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, military affairs were urgent and the Works Ministry needed talent; Jing was transferred to director of construction in the Works Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianqi, military affairs were urgent and the Works Ministry needed talent; Jing was transferred to director of construction in the Works Ministry.

sentences.zh: 督治九門垣墉，市銅江南，皆勤於其職。

translations.literal: He supervised repair of the walls and ramparts of the nine gates and procured copper in Jiangnan—diligent in his duties throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised repair of the walls and ramparts of the nine gates and procured copper in Jiangnan—diligent in his duties throughout.

sentences.zh: 遷虞衡員外郎，司鼓鑄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Forestry and Timber and oversaw bell and coin casting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Forestry and Timber and oversaw bell and coin casting.

sentences.zh: 時慶陵大工未竣，費不貲。

translations.literal: At that time the great works at Qingling were not yet finished, and the expense was incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the great works at Qingling were not yet finished, and the expense was incalculable.

sentences.zh: 燝知內府廢銅山積，可發以助鑄，移牒內官監言之。

translations.literal: Jing knew the inner palace had mountains of scrap copper piled up that could be released to aid casting; he sent an official letter to the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs stating this.
translations.idiomatic: Jing knew the inner palace had mountains of scrap copper piled up that could be released to aid casting; he sent an official letter to the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs stating this.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢怒，不發，燝遂具疏以請。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian was angered and would not release it; Jing then submitted a full memorial requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was angered and would not release it; Jing then submitted a full memorial requesting it.

sentences.zh: 忠賢益怒，假中旨詰責。

translations.literal: Zhongxian grew angrier still and, using a forged edict from the inner palace, rebuked and censured him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian grew angrier still and, using a forged edict from the inner palace, rebuked and censured him.

sentences.zh: 燝旋進屯田郎中，督陵務。

translations.literal: Jing was soon promoted to director of garrison fields and supervised tomb works.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was soon promoted to director of garrison fields and supervised tomb works.

sentences.zh: 其時，忠賢益肆，廷臣楊漣等交擊，率被嚴旨。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongxian grew all the more unrestrained; court officials such as Yang Lian attacked him in turn and mostly received stern edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Zhongxian grew all the more unrestrained; court officials such as Yang Lian attacked him in turn and mostly received stern edicts.

sentences.zh: 燝憤，抗章極論，略言：「人主有政權，有利權，不可委臣下，況刑余寺人哉？

translations.literal: Jing, indignant, submitted a defiant memorial arguing to the utmost, stating in part: "The ruler has governmental authority and fiscal authority—they must not be entrusted to ministers, much less to castrated palace eunuchs!
translations.idiomatic: Jing, indignant, submitted a defiant memorial arguing to the utmost, stating in part: "The ruler holds governmental authority and fiscal authority—they must not be entrusted to ministers, much less to castrated palace eunuchs!

sentences.zh: 忠賢性狡而貪，膽粗而大，口銜天憲，手握王爵，所好生羽毛，所惡成瘡痏。

translations.literal: Zhongxian is cunning by nature and greedy, bold and brazen; he holds heaven's edicts in his mouth and grasps princely ranks in his hand—what he favors grows feathers, what he hates becomes sores.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian is cunning and greedy, bold and brazen; he holds heaven's edicts in his mouth and princely ranks in his hand—what he favors grows feathers, what he hates becomes sores.

sentences.zh: 蔭子弟，則一世再世；

translations.literal: To ennoble sons and nephews—one generation, then two;
translations.idiomatic: To ennoble sons and nephews—one generation, then two;

sentences.zh: 賚廝養，則千金萬金。

translations.literal: to reward servants and attendants—a thousand gold, ten thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: to reward servants and attendants—a thousand gold, ten thousand gold.

sentences.zh: 毒痡士庶，斃百余人；

translations.literal: He poisons and cripples scholars and commoners, killing more than a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: He poisons and cripples scholars and commoners, killing more than a hundred;

sentences.zh: 威加搢紳，空十數署。

translations.literal: his authority presses upon the gentry and officials, emptying more than ten offices.
translations.idiomatic: his authority presses upon the gentry and officials, emptying more than ten offices.

sentences.zh: 一切生殺予奪之權盡為忠賢所竊，陛下猶不覺悟乎？

translations.literal: All power of life, death, grant, and seizure has been stolen by Zhongxian—is Your Majesty still not awakened?
translations.idiomatic: All power of life, death, grant, and seizure has been stolen by Wei Zhongxian—is Your Majesty still not awakened?

sentences.zh: 且忠賢固供事先帝者也，陛下之寵忠賢，亦以忠賢曾供事先帝也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhongxian originally served the late emperor; Your Majesty's favor for Zhongxian is also because Zhongxian once served the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wei Zhongxian originally served the late emperor; Your Majesty's favor for him is also because he once served the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 乃於先帝陵工，略不厝念。

translations.literal: Yet regarding the late emperor's tomb works, he scarcely spares a thought.
translations.idiomatic: Yet regarding the late emperor's tomb works, he scarcely spares a thought.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗屢請銅，靳不肯予。

translations.literal: Your subject repeatedly requested copper, but he begrudged and would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: I repeatedly requested copper, but he begrudged and would not grant it.

sentences.zh: 間過香山碧雲寺，見忠賢自營墳墓，其規制弘敞，擬於陵寢。

translations.literal: Once, passing Xiangshan and Biyun Temple, I saw Zhongxian building his own tomb—its scale grand and spacious, modeled on an imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing Xiangshan and Biyun Temple, I saw Wei Zhongxian building his own tomb—its scale grand and spacious, modeled on an imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 前列生祠，又前建佛宇，璇題耀日，珠網懸星，費金錢幾百萬。
