translations.literal: Before it stood a living shrine, and before that a Buddhist hall; inscribed plaques dazzled in the sun, pearl nets hung like stars—the cost in gold and silver ran to several million.
translations.idiomatic: Before it stood a living shrine, and before that a Buddhist hall; inscribed plaques dazzled in the sun, pearl nets hung like stars—the cost in gold and silver ran to several million.

sentences.zh: 為己墳墓則如此，為先帝陵寢則如彼，可勝誅哉！

translations.literal: For his own tomb it was thus; for the late emperor's tomb it was as that—can this not be condemned?
translations.idiomatic: For his own tomb it was thus; for the late emperor's tomb it was as that—can this not be condemned?

sentences.zh: 今忠賢已盡竊陛下權，致內廷外朝止知有忠賢，不知有陛下，尚可一日留左右耶？」

translations.literal: Now Zhongxian has fully stolen Your Majesty's authority, so that inner court and outer court know only Zhongxian and not Your Majesty—can he still be kept at your side for one day?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Wei Zhongxian has fully stolen Your Majesty's authority, so that inner court and outer court know only Wei Zhongxian and not Your Majesty—can he still be kept at your side for one day?

sentences.zh: 疏入，忠賢大怒，矯旨廷杖一百，斥為民。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Zhongxian was greatly angered and forged an edict for a court beating of one hundred strokes and dismissal as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Wei Zhongxian was greatly angered and forged an edict for a court beating of one hundred strokes and dismissal as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 執政言官論救，皆不聽。

translations.literal: The chief ministers and remonstrating officials argued for his rescue, but none was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers and remonstrating officials argued for his rescue, but none was heeded.

sentences.zh: 當是時，忠賢惡廷臣交章劾己，無所發忿，思借燝立威。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongxian hated that court officials submitted memorial after memorial impeaching him with nowhere to vent his rage; he wished to use Jing to establish his authority.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Zhongxian hated that court officials submitted memorial after memorial impeaching him with nowhere to vent his rage; he wished to use Jing to establish his authority.

sentences.zh: 乃命群奄至燝邸，摔而毆之，比至闕下，氣息才屬。

translations.literal: He then ordered a crowd of eunuchs to Jing's residence, threw him down and beat him; by the time they reached below the palace gate, his breath barely remained.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered a crowd of eunuchs to Jing's residence, threw him down and beat him; by the time they reached below the palace gate, his breath barely remained.

sentences.zh: 杖已，絕而復蘇。

translations.literal: After the beating he died and revived.
translations.idiomatic: After the beating he died and revived.

sentences.zh: 群奄更肆蹴踏，越四日即卒，時四年七月七日也。

translations.literal: The crowd of eunuchs trampled him all the more fiercely; within four days he died—on the seventh day of the seventh month of the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd of eunuchs trampled him all the more fiercely; within four days he died—on the seventh day of the seventh month of the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 忠賢恨猶不置，羅織其罪，誣以贓賄三百。

translations.literal: Zhongxian's hatred was still not satisfied; he fabricated charges and falsely accused him of embezzlement and bribery of three hundred taels.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's hatred was still not satisfied; he fabricated charges and falsely accused him of embezzlement and bribery of three hundred taels.

sentences.zh: 燝廉吏，破產乃竣。

translations.literal: Jing was an incorrupt official; his family was ruined before the case was closed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was an incorrupt official; his family was ruined before the case was closed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈光祿卿，官其一子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and one son was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and one son was granted office.

sentences.zh: 福王時，謚忠貞。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, he was given the posthumous title Zhongzhen—Loyal and Chaste.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, he was given the posthumous title Zhongzhen—Loyal and Chaste.

sentences.zh: 燝杖死未幾，巡城御史福清林汝翥嘗笞內侍曹進、傅國興，忠賢矯旨杖汝翥如燝。

translations.literal: Not long after Jing was beaten to death, city-inspecting censor Lin Ruhu of Fuqing had once flogged inner attendants Cao Jin and Fu Guoxing; Zhongxian forged an edict to beat Ruhu as with Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after Jing was beaten to death, city-inspecting censor Lin Ruhu of Fuqing had once flogged inner attendants Cao Jin and Fu Guoxing; Wei Zhongxian forged an edict to beat Ruhu as with Jing.

sentences.zh: 汝翥懼，逃之遵化，自歸於巡撫鄧渼。

translations.literal: Ruhu, afraid, fled to Zunhua and surrendered himself to grand coordinator Deng Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhu, afraid, fled to Zunhua and surrendered himself to grand coordinator Deng Mei.

sentences.zh: 渼以聞，卒杖之。

translations.literal: Mei reported this, and in the end Ruhu was beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Mei reported this, and in the end Ruhu was beaten.

sentences.zh: 汝翥起家鄉舉，知沛縣，徐鴻儒攻沛甚急，堅守不下，由此擢御史。

translations.literal: Ruhu rose from a provincial graduate, served as magistrate of Pei County, and when Xu Hongru attacked Pei with great urgency held firm and did not fall—by this he was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhu rose from a provincial graduate, served as magistrate of Pei County, and when Xu Hongru attacked Pei with great urgency held firm and did not fall—by this he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，仕至浙江副使。

translations.literal: Under Chongzhen he rose to vice commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he rose to vice commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 汝翥雖受杖，幸不死。

translations.literal: Although Ruhu was beaten, he fortunately did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Although Ruhu was beaten, he fortunately did not die.

sentences.zh: 而是時，丁乾學、夏之令、吳裕中、劉鐸、吳懷賢、蘇繼歐、張汶諸人，皆忤忠賢致死。

translations.literal: But at that time Ding Ganxue, Xia Zhiling, Wu Yuzhong, Liu Duo, Wu Huaixian, Su Ji'ou, and Zhang Wen—all who offended Zhongxian—died.
translations.idiomatic: But at that time Ding Ganxue, Xia Zhiling, Wu Yuzhong, Liu Duo, Wu Huaixian, Su Ji'ou, and Zhang Wen—all who offended Wei Zhongxian—met their deaths.

sentences.zh: 乾學，浙江山陰人，寄籍京師，官檢討。

translations.literal: Ganxue was a native of Shanyin, Zhejiang, with registered residence in the capital, and served as reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Ganxue was a native of Shanyin, Zhejiang, with registered residence in the capital, and served as reviser.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，偕給事中郝土膏典試江西，發策刺忠賢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi, together with supervising secretary Hao Tugao he presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination and set examination questions that satirized Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianqi, together with supervising secretary Hao Tugao he presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination and set examination questions that satirized Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 忠賢怒，矯旨鐫三秩，復除其名。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was angered and forged an edict demoting him three ranks and then removing his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was angered and forged an edict demoting him three ranks and then removing his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 已，使人詐為校尉往逮，挫辱之，竟憤郁而卒。

translations.literal: Afterward, he sent men disguised as guards to arrest him, humiliated him, and in the end Ganxue died of indignant depression.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he sent men disguised as guards to arrest him, humiliated him, and in the end Ganxue died of indignant depression.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈侍讀學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 之令，光山人。

translations.literal: Zhiling was a native of Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiling was a native of Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 知攸、歙二縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of You and She counties and was summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of You and She counties and was summoned and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏論邊事，力詆毛文龍不足恃。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial discussing frontier affairs, forcefully denouncing Mao Wenlong as unworthy of reliance.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial discussing frontier affairs, forcefully denouncing Mao Wenlong as unworthy of reliance.

sentences.zh: 忠賢庇文龍，傳旨削之令籍，閣臣救免。

translations.literal: Zhongxian shielded Wenlong and transmitted an edict stripping Zhiling from the rolls; grand secretaries intervened and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian shielded Wenlong and transmitted an edict stripping Zhiling from the rolls; grand secretaries intervened and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 及巡皇城，內使馮忠等犯法，劾治之，益為忠賢所銜，崔呈秀亦以事銜之。

translations.literal: When inspecting the imperial city, he found inner attendants Feng Zhong and others violating the law and impeached and punished them; this made Zhongxian hate him all the more, and Cui Chengxiu also bore a grudge over an affair.
translations.idiomatic: When inspecting the imperial city, he found inner attendants Feng Zhong and others violating the law and impeached and punished them; this made Wei Zhongxian hate him all the more, and Cui Chengxiu also bore a grudge over an affair.

sentences.zh: 遂屬御史卓邁劾之令黨比熊廷弼，有詔削奪。

translations.literal: Thereupon investigating censor Zhuo Mai was set to impeach Zhiling for factional ties with Xiong Tingbi, and an edict stripped and confiscated his honors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon investigating censor Zhuo Mai was set to impeach Zhiling for factional ties with Xiong Tingbi, and an edict stripped and confiscated his honors.

sentences.zh: 頃之，御史倪文煥復劾之令計陷文龍，幾誤疆事。

translations.literal: Before long, investigating censor Ni Wenhuan again impeached Zhiling for scheming against Wenlong and nearly ruining frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, investigating censor Ni Wenhuan again impeached Zhiling for scheming against Wenlong and nearly ruining frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 遂逮下詔獄，坐贓拷死。

translations.literal: He was then arrested and thrown into the imperial prison, convicted of embezzlement, and beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested, thrown into the imperial prison on a charge of embezzlement, and tortured to death.

sentences.zh: 裕中，江夏人。

translations.literal: Yuzhong was a native of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuzhong was a native of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 為順德知縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Shunde and was summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Shunde, then was summoned to the capital and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 大學士丁紹軾陷熊廷弼死，裕中有疏詆紹軾。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ding Shaozhi framed Xiong Tingbi to his death; Yuzhong had a memorial denouncing Shaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ding Shaozhi framed Xiong Tingbi to his death; Yuzhong submitted a memorial denouncing Shaozhi.

sentences.zh: 忠賢傳旨詰裕中為廷弼姻戚，代之報仇，廷杖一百，創重卒。

translations.literal: Zhongxian transmitted an edict rebuking Yuzhong as Xiong Tingbi's in-law seeking revenge for him; he received a court beating of one hundred strokes and died from severe wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian transmitted an edict rebuking Yuzhong as Xiong Tingbi's in-law seeking revenge for him; he received a court beating of one hundred strokes and died from severe wounds.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，賜贈蔭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, posthumous honors and hereditary privilege were granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he received posthumous honors and hereditary privilege for a son.

sentences.zh: 鐸，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Duo was a native of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Duo was a native of Luling.

sentences.zh: 由刑部郎中為揚州知府。

translations.literal: From director in the Ministry of Justice he became prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from director in the Ministry of Justice, he became prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 憤忠賢亂政，作詩書僧扇，有「陰霾國事非」句，偵者得之，聞於忠賢。

translations.literal: Angered at Zhongxian's disorderly rule, he wrote a poem on a monk's fan with the line "dark clouds hang over state affairs—wrong!"; spies obtained it and reported it to Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Angered at Wei Zhongxian's disorderly rule, he wrote a poem on a monk's fan with the line "dark clouds hang over state affairs—wrong!"; spies obtained it and reported it to Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 倪文煥者，揚州人也，素銜鐸，遂嗾忠賢逮治之。

translations.literal: Ni Wenhuan was a native of Yangzhou who had long borne a grudge against Duo and thus incited Zhongxian to arrest and punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Wenhuan was a native of Yangzhou who had long borne a grudge against Duo and thus incited Wei Zhongxian to arrest and punish him.

sentences.zh: 鐸雅善忠賢子良卿，事獲解，許還故官。

translations.literal: Duo was on good terms with Zhongxian's son Liangqing; the affair was resolved and he was permitted to return to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was on good terms with Wei Zhongxian's son Liangqing; the affair was resolved and he was permitted to return to his former office.

sentences.zh: 良卿從容問鐸：「曩錦衣往逮，索金幾何？」

translations.literal: Liangqing casually asked Duo: "When the Embroidered Uniform Guard came to arrest you before, how much gold did they demand?"
translations.idiomatic: Liangqing casually asked Duo: "When the Embroidered Uniform Guard came to arrest you earlier, how much gold did they demand?

sentences.zh: 曰：「三千金耳。」

translations.literal: He said: "Three thousand gold only."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Three thousand taels only."

sentences.zh: 良卿令錦衣還之。

translations.literal: Liangqing ordered the guard to return it.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqing ordered the guard to return it.

sentences.zh: 其人怒，日夜伺鐸隙，言鐸系獄時，與囚方震孺同謀居間，遂再下獄。

translations.literal: That man, enraged, day and night watched for Duo's openings, saying that when Duo was imprisoned he conspired with the prisoner Fang Zhenru as intermediaries, and Duo was again thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: That man, enraged, day and night watched for an opening against Duo, claiming that while Duo was imprisoned he had conspired with the prisoner Fang Zhenru as go-between, and Duo was again thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 會鐸家人有夜醮者，參將張體乾誣鐸咒詛忠賢，刑部尚書薛貞坐以大辟。

translations.literal: It happened that Duo's family held a night ritual; Brigadier Zhang Tigang falsely accused Duo of cursing Zhongxian, and Minister of Justice Xue Zhen sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Duo's family held a night ritual; Brigadier Zhang Tigan falsely accused Duo of cursing Wei Zhongxian, and Minister of Justice Xue Zhen sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 忠賢誅，貞、體乾並抵罪，鐸贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian was executed, Zhen and Tigang both received punishment, and Duo was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian was executed, Zhen and Tigang both received punishment, and Duo was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 懷賢，休寧人。

translations.literal: Huaixian was a native of Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Huaixian was a native of Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 由國子監生授內閣中書舍人。

translations.literal: From a student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from a student of the Imperial Academy, he was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 同官傅應升者，忠賢甥也，懷賢遇之無加禮，應升恨之。

translations.literal: His colleague Fu Yingsheng was Zhongxian's nephew; Huaixian did not treat him with extra courtesy, and Yingsheng resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Fu Yingsheng was Wei Zhongxian's nephew; Huaixian did not treat him with extra courtesy, and Yingsheng resented him.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾忠賢疏出，懷賢書其上曰：「宜如韓魏公治任守忠故事，即時遣戍。」

translations.literal: When Yang Lian's impeachment memorial against Zhongxian came out, Huaixian wrote upon it: "One should follow the precedent of Han Wei Gong's treatment of Ren Shouzhong—immediately banish to garrison duty."
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian's impeachment memorial against Wei Zhongxian came out, Huaixian wrote upon it: "One should follow the precedent of Han Qi's treatment of Ren Shouzhong—immediately banish him to garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 又與工部主事吳昌期書，有「事極必反，反正不遠」語。

translations.literal: He also wrote to Works Ministry director Wu Changqi with the words "when affairs reach the extreme they must reverse; the reversal is not far."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Works Ministry director Wu Changqi with the words "when affairs reach the extreme they must reverse; the reversal is not far."

sentences.zh: 忠賢偵知之，大怒曰：「何物小吏，亦敢謗我！」

translations.literal: Zhongxian learned through spies and raged: "What kind of petty clerk dares slander me!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian learned through spies and raged: "What kind of petty clerk dares slander me!

sentences.zh: 遂矯旨下詔獄，坐以結納汪文言，為左光鬥、魏大中鷹犬，拷掠死。

translations.literal: He then forged an edict and threw him into the imperial prison, convicted of associating with Wang Wényan and serving as hawk and hound to Zuo Guangdou and Wei Dazhong, and tortured him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He then forged an edict and threw him into the imperial prison, convicted of associating with Wang Wényan and serving as hawk and hound to Zuo Guangdou and Wei Dazhong, and tortured him to death.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈工部主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as director in the Works Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously granted the rank of director in the Works Ministry.

sentences.zh: 繼歐，許州人。

translations.literal: Ji'ou was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ji'ou was a native of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷知元氏、真定、柏鄉，入為吏部稽勛主事，累遷考功郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Yuanshi, Zhending, and Baixiang; entered as director of merit records in the Ministry of Personnel; and was promoted in turn to director in the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Yuanshi, Zhending, and Baixiang; entered the Ministry of Personnel as director of merit records; and rose in turn to director in the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 將調文選，中旨謂為楊漣私黨，削籍歸。

translations.literal: When about to be transferred to the Bureau of Appointments, an inner edict said he was Yang Lian's private partisan; he was struck from the rolls and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When about to be transferred to the Bureau of Appointments, an inner edict declared him Yang Lian's private partisan; he was struck from the rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 時緹騎四出，同里副使孫織錦素附忠賢，遣人怵繼歐曰：「逮者至矣。」

translations.literal: At that time mounted arrest guards ranged everywhere; his fellow townsman Vice Commissioner Sun Zhijin had long attached himself to Zhongxian and sent a man to threaten Ji'ou: "The arresting officers have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: At that time mounted arrest guards ranged everywhere; his fellow townsman Vice Commissioner Sun Zhijin had long attached himself to Wei Zhongxian and sent a man to threaten Ji'ou: "The arresting officers have arrived.

sentences.zh: 繼歐自經死。

translations.literal: Ji'ou hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'ou hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太常寺卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was posthumously granted the title Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 汶，邯鄲人。

translations.literal: Wen was a native of Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen was a native of Handan.

sentences.zh: 尚書國彥曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Minister Guo Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of the minister Guo Yan.

sentences.zh: 由蔭敘為後軍都督府經歷。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was appointed administrator in the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he entered service as administrator in the Rear Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 嘗被酒詆忠賢，下獄拷掠死。

translations.literal: Once, drunk, he denounced Zhongxian; he was thrown into prison and tortured to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drunk, he denounced Wei Zhongxian; he was thrown into prison and tortured to death.

sentences.zh: 亦獲贈恤。

translations.literal: He also received posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: He too received posthumous honors and mourning gifts.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：自古閹宦之甘心善類者，莫甚於漢、唐之季，然皆倉卒一時，為自救計耳。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: From of old, among eunuchs who set their hearts on destroying worthy men, none surpassed those at the end of Han and Tang—yet all acted in haste for a moment, as plans for self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist says: From of old, among eunuchs who set their hearts on destroying worthy men, none surpassed those at the end of Han and Tang—yet even they acted in haste for a moment, as plans for self-preservation.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢之殺諸人也，揚毒焰以快其私，肆無忌憚。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian's killing of these men spread poisonous flames to gratify his private ends, reckless and without scruple.
translations.idiomatic: In killing these men, Wei Zhongxian spread poisonous flames to gratify his private ends, reckless and without scruple.

sentences.zh: 蓋主荒政比之余，公道淪亡，人心敗壞，兇氣參會，群邪翕謀，故搢紳之禍烈於前古。

translations.literal: It was because amid the ruler's neglect of government, public right was lost, men's hearts corrupted, violent airs converged, and a host of villains joined in conspiracy that the calamity of the gentry exceeded that of earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: This was because amid the ruler's neglect of government, public right collapsed, men's hearts rotted, violent airs converged, and a host of villains joined in conspiracy—so the calamity of the gentry exceeded that of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 諸人之受禍也，酷矣哉！

translations.literal: The calamity these men suffered—how bitter!
translations.idiomatic: How bitter was the calamity these men suffered!
